title: TWIX: a Two-Stage Approach for End-To-End Named Entity Recognition and Relation Extraction
abstract: The exponential growth of scientific publications calls for automatic Information Extraction (IE) systems to support knowledge discovery. In this context, the GutBrainIE benchmark evaluates Named Entity Recognition (NER), Named Entity Recognition and Disambiguation (NERD), and Relation Extraction (RE) systems in the gut-brain axis domain. We propose Two-stage Workflow for Information eXtraction (TWIX), an end-to-end IE pipeline featuring three interconnected modules, each leveraging a two-stage framework to solve all four GutBrainIE subtasks. Evaluation on the development and test sets shows that our method substantially outperforms the baseline by a wide margin, while also ranking first among all participant submissions across all subtasks. These results indicate that the proposed two-stage pipeline effectively improves both precision and recall in practical settings.

title: BeamRMX: Radiation-Pattern-Driven Learning for Generalizable Beam Radio Map Prediction and Beam Management
abstract: The evolution toward sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks is driving larger antenna arrays and highly directional multi-beam transmission, making accurate knowledge of beam-dependent spatial coverage important for beam management and environment-aware network operation. Radio maps (RMs) provide such a representation, yet conventional RM prediction assumes omnidirectional or transmitter-level radiation. In beamformed multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems, one propagation scene instead gives rise to many configuration-dependent beam radio maps (BeamRMs), creating challenges in beam representation and generalization. Existing methods either condition prediction on beam descriptors or use beam maps as auxiliary inputs to generic architectures. We propose BeamRMX, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first dedicated framework to treat the spatial radiation pattern as the primary BeamRM query and learn how scene geometry transforms it into the received power field. XBase learns multiscale interactions between the radiation query and scene geometry, while an optional Evidence Adapter uses a few cross-configuration BeamRMs from the same scene. Matched-domain and zero-shot experiments show consistent gains over deterministic and diffusion baselines, including mean absolute error reductions of 26.1\% on unseen scenes and 47.8\% on an unseen configuration. Cross-configuration evidence further improves reconstruction and intra-sector beam refinement.

title: A Runtime Decentralized Attestation and Coordinated Repair Framework for Securing Automotive ECUs
abstract: The evolution of automotive technology increasingly integrates components, transforming vehicles into interconnected systems of systems. Modern vehicles are controlled by a distributed system of computing devices, known as electronic control units (ECUs). However, this interconnectedness means that any error poses significant risks to the vehicle operator. In particular, malware can be injected into ECUs, threatening vehicle safety. To address this, we need mechanisms to detect compromised ECUs then repair them to a benign state. Existing approaches mainly focus on detection and do not address the challenge of integrating detection with runtime ECU repair. This integration is nontrivial because runtime repair involves both local rollback and reboot with timing determined from global vehicle context to avoid unsafe behavior. In this work, we have designed DACER, a runtime decentralized attestation and coordinated repair framework for automotive ECUs. DACER is the first approach that co-designs attestation and repair to unify the ``local'' nature of firmware rollback with the ``global'' nature of ECU reboot. In DACER, each ECU performs efficient local self-attestation and self-repair functions, enabling low-overhead coordination for distributed operations. In addition, DACER takes advantage of the hierarchical vehicle computing architecture. Our resulting DACER design checks the entire state of the vehicle, resists single points of failure, conforms to real-time constraints, and enables firmware restoration during runtime. The key functions are enabled by the ARM TrustZone equipped within each ECU and the secure flash memory controller embedded in the storage device. We implemented DACER on real-world hardware and experimentally demonstrated its low overhead.

title: Resumen de GenSIE en IberLEF 2026: extracción de información guiada por esquemas con modelos de lenguaje pequeños en español
abstract: GenSIE is the IberLEF 2026 shared task on schema-guided information extraction from Spanish text with small language models. A CPU-only system receives a (text, instruction, JSON schema) triple and must emit a schema-conformant object faithful to the text, returning null for fields the text does not support. We contribute a 271-instance Spanish development benchmark over eight domains, a 145-instance held-out gold test set that adds a ninth, a semi-automatic agentic curation pipeline with three human gates, and an evaluator pairing micro-F1 over flattened schemas with a multi-model gap-closed metric. Eleven teams submitted thirty-five pipelines, scored on 125 instances against no-think baselines (Gemma 4 E4B F1=0.7780, Qwen3-14B F1=0.7542). DRILLER leads, closing 27.7% of the baseline-to-perfect gap, though a paired bootstrap cannot separate the top three. Retrieval and schema enrichment pay off; extra inference passes do not.

title: Frequency-definite photon pairs from a Lithium Niobate waveguide resonator
abstract: Quantum light sources that will be embedded in future quantum networks like for example in long distance communication need to fulfil a versatile range of requirements. Most importantly, low propagation losses and a good time synchronization between the remote nodes are required. Additional constrains will be provided by other hardware components like the quantum memories that so far exist only for narrow spectral bandwidths. We present here a pulsed quantum light source based on parametric down-conversion in a periodically-poled Lithium Niobate waveguide (PPLN-WG) resonator. The end facets of the PPLN-WG are coated with a high reflection coating forming a Fabry-Perot Resonator (FPR). Our source works at the well-established telecommunication C-Band and produces in pulsed operation photon pairs with a 2GHz bandwidth. Here, we present a thorough investigation of the FPR, its bandwidth, the group indices of the PPLN-WG, as well as the temporal pulse shapes of the photon pairs paving our way towards the generation of the time-bin entanglement.

title: Penerapan Hash Table dalam Sistem Penyimpanan Data Buku Perpustakaan Ibrahimy Berbasis Komputer
abstract: Temu balik berdasarkan kode buku merupakan operasi yang sering dilakukan ketika sistem mengakses, memperbarui, atau menghapus metadata. Jika pencarian dilakukan dengan menelusuri elemen satu per satu, waktu proses cenderung bertambah ketika jumlah record meningkat. Penelitian ini mengevaluasi Hash Table dengan separate chaining untuk pencarian exact-key dan membandingkannya dengan sequential search pada ArrayList, java.util. HashMap, dan java.util. TreeMap. Eksperimen menggunakan 10.000 record sintetis; dataset ini dipilih agar dapat dibangkitkan ulang dan tidak dimaksudkan sebagai representasi koleksi aktual Perpustakaan Ibrahimy. Empat target load factor (0,50; 0,75; 1,00; dan 1,50) diuji dengan 20.000 query yang terdiri atas 80% hit dan 20% miss. Setelah 10 putaran warm-up, setiap konfigurasi diukur 30 kali menggunakan System.nanoTime(); hasil dianalisis melalui rata-rata, simpangan baku, interval kepercayaan 95%, collision, panjang chain, dan speedup. Sequential search mencatat rata-rata 518,195 ms, TreeMap 3,979 ms, HashMap 0,817 ms, sedangkan Hash Table chaining berada pada 0,729-0,916 ms. Ketika load factor meningkat dari 0,50 menjadi 1,50, item collision naik dari 21,53% menjadi 48,26% dan panjang chain maksimum dari 5 menjadi 9. Pada workload ini, struktur berbasis hash memberikan waktu pencarian yang jauh lebih rendah daripada sequential search. Load factor 0,75 memberi kompromi yang layak antara kapasitas bucket dan latensi, tetapi kesimpulan ini dibatasi pada dataset, pola query, dan lingkungan pengujian yang digunakan.

title: A Federated Deep Learning Framework for Privacy-Preserving IoT-Based Healthcare Monitoring Systems
abstract: Continuous, remote patient monitoring is now practically possible thanks to the expanding use of wearable and bedside sensors enabled by the Internet of Things (IoT). However, the centralised aggregation of physiological data needed by traditional deep learning pipelines presents significant privacy, legal, and bandwidth issues. In order to build a shared diagnostic model across dispersed IoT healthcare nodes without sending raw patient data to a central server, this study suggests a federated deep learning (FDL) system. The framework integrates a FedAvg/FedProx aggregation scheme at the server with a lightweight hybrid convolutional neural network and bidirectional long short-term memory (CNN-BiLSTM) architecture for local physiological-signal feature extraction. Differential privacy (DP) noise injection and secure aggregation are added to prevent information leakage from shared gradients. We present a simulation-based evaluation intended to characterise the expected accuracy, communication-efficiency, and privacy-utility trade-offs of the framework in comparison to centralised and local-only baselines. We also describe the end-to-end system architecture, the on-device training and communication protocol, and the privacy-accounting method. The results show that the suggested federated strategy can reduce per-round communication volume by an order of magnitude, eliminate the need to transmit raw sensor data, and approach centralized-training accuracy within a narrow margin. We also examine how the differential-privacy budget affects model utility and talk about unresolved issues with adversarial robustness, device and network heterogeneity, and statistical heterogeneity (nonIID data). The suggested approach provides a workable blueprint for scalable, privacypreserving, and regulator-compliant AI-based healthcare monitoring at the network edge.

title: Rewards, Regrets, and Rubber Arms: A Critical Survey Review of Reinforcement Learning in Games and Robotics
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Reinforcement Learning in Games and Robotics in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of reinforcement learning and robotics as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Evaluation Datasets for "Understanding the Privacy-Preserving Potential of HTTP/2 Against Webpage Fingerprinting"
abstract: Evaluation Artifacts and Datasets for "Understanding the Privacy-Preserving Potential of HTTP/2 Against Webpage Fingerprinting" This record contains the evaluation datasets and supporting artifacts for the paper "Understanding the Privacy-Preserving Potential of HTTP/2 Against Webpage Fingerprinting", accepted at ACM CCS 2026. The Zenodo record contains: raw browser traces used as input to the replay framework; processed evaluation datasets for the selected calibrated defenses; benchmark-result artifacts for the selected calibrated defenses; and bandwidth and latency overhead measurements. The substantially larger raw replay corpus, including the defense-calibration sweeps, is provided separately through Google Drive as described below. Included datasets We evaluate five webpage datasets: 1_amazon - Amazon 2_bbc - BBC 3_reddit -- Reddit 4_udemy -- Udemy 5_wiki -- Wikipedia Files Browser traces `browser_traces.tar.zst`: Raw browser traces used as input to the replay framework. These traces contain the browser-collected inputs required to regenerate the replay-based datasets. Calibrated-defense evaluation artifacts For each of the five datasets, three archives are provided: datasets_calibrated_defenses_{dataset}_benchmarks.tar.zstdatasets_calibrated_defenses_{dataset}_deepsetraces.tar.zstdatasets_calibrated_defenses_{dataset}_wefdetraces.tar.zstHere, {dataset} is one of: 1_amazon, 2_bbc, 3_reddit, 4_udemy, 5_wiki For example: datasets_calibrated_defenses_4_udemy_benchmarks.tar.zstdatasets_calibrated_defenses_4_udemy_deepsetraces.tar.zstdatasets_calibrated_defenses_4_udemy_wefdetraces.tar.zst The archive types are: `benchmarks`: benchmark-result artifacts for the evaluated fingerprinting attacks. `deepsetraces`: neural-network trace representation used by DF, VarCNN, Holmes, RobustFP-CNN, and DeepSE-WF. `wefdetraces`: handcrafted-feature representation used by k-FP and WeFDE. Each archive is further organized by defense. For example, a WeFDE archive contains entries such as: front/tcp_repr/front_wefdetraces.tar.zsth2pc/tcp_repr/h2pc_wefdetraces.tar.zsthttpos/tcp_repr/httpos_wefdetraces.tar.zstllama/tcp_repr/llama_wefdetraces.tar.zst...The nested archives contain the evaluation data for the corresponding defense. Overhead analysis `overhead_analysis.tar.zst`: Contains the measured bandwidth and latency overhead data used in the privacy--overhead analysis. The archive contains one nested archive per dataset: 1_amazon.tar.zst, 2_bbc.tar.zst, 3_reddit.tar.zst, 4_udemy.tar.zst, 5_wiki.tar.zst, Each dataset archive contains the corresponding per-defense overhead measurements, including: overhead/overhead_summary.csvoverhead/tradeoff_yvalues.jsonoverhead/ovh_*.csv Extracting the data The files use Zstandard-compressed tar archives (`.tar.zst`). An archive can be listed without extraction using: tar --zstd -tf ARCHIVE.tar.zst For example, to inspect the Udemy WeFDE archive: tar --zstd -tf datasets_calibrated_defenses_4_udemy_wefdetraces.tar.zst The artifact repository accompanying the paper provides `prepare_workspace.sh`, which prepares an evaluation workspace for a selected dataset and either one defense, multiple defenses, or all available defenses. Full raw replay dataset The processed calibrated-defense evaluation datasets used for the benchmarking experiments are included in this Zenodo record. The much larger raw replay collection is hosted separately on Google Drive. It contains: raw replay traces generated during the defense-parameter calibration sweeps; and raw replay traces generated using the selected calibrated defense configurations. The complete raw replay collection is available at: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1WAHwUJq44IQcHiTpsyAl8bgUvORlD2xR?usp=sharing Code The source code for dataset generation, defense calibration, benchmarking, and the `wfaudit` auditing tool is available at: https://github.com/bcebere/Understanding-the-Privacy-Preserving-Potential-of-HTTP2-Against-Webpage-Fingerprinting Citation If you use these datasets or artifacts, please cite the associated paper: @inproceedings{cebere2026http2wf, author = {Bogdan Constantin Cebere and Prateek Kumar and Sylvain Chatel and Wouter Lueks and Christian Rossow}, title = {Understanding the Privacy-Preserving Potential of {HTTP/2} Against Webpage Fingerprinting}, booktitle = {Proceedings of the 2026 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS '26)}, year = {2026}, month = nov, publisher = {Association for Computing Machinery}, address = {New York, NY, USA}, location = {The Hague, Netherlands}, note = {November 15--19, 2026}, doi = {10.1145/3830454.3846538}}

title: Quantum Key Distribution Based on Quantum Depolarization
abstract: This paper proposes a novel distributed key distribution (DKD) scheme leveraging the principles of quantum depolarization. The core claim centers on enhancing the security of DKD protocols by exploiting the inherent properties of quantum depolarization processes. The proposed mechanism utilizes the quantum depolarization inherent in existing DKD protocols to effectively eliminate eavesdropping attempts targeting the key. This work focuses on improving the resilience of DKD systems against attacks by introducing a controlled depolarization process, thereby making key interception significantly more difficult. The scheme's effectiveness is demonstrated through a theoretical analysis, outlining the mathematical framework and security considerations. The design incorporates elements of the Bennett-Mayhew protocol, modified to incorporate a controlled depolarization step. We present a mathematical formulation detailing the key generation process and the security proof, highlighting the reduced key error rate under realistic depolarization scenarios. The proposed approach represents a significant advancement in DKD security, offering a robust defense against evolving quantum attacks.

title: Quantum State Non-Euclidean Simulation
abstract: Quantum state non-Euclidean simulation aims to provide a more precise and nuanced understanding of quantum states by leveraging the unique properties of non-Euclidean geometry. This paper explores a novel algorithm for simulating quantum states, focusing on the interplay between quantum entanglement and non-Euclidean geometry to model state evolution. The core mechanism involves integrating quantum entanglement with non-Euclidean geometric structures, offering a potential pathway to enhanced quantum state simulation and prediction. Traditional quantum simulation methods predominantly operate within Euclidean spaces, highlighting the need for a framework capable of handling the complexities introduced by non-Euclidean geometries. The proposed algorithm represents a significant advancement, potentially unlocking deeper insights into quantum mechanics.

title: 基于自适应的量子纠错算法
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense promise for advancements across diverse fields, from drug discovery and materials science to financial modeling and cryptography. However, the inherent fragility of quantum states necessitates robust quantum error correction techniques. Current quantum error correction methods, while effective, often rely on computationally intensive and time-consuming procedures. This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum error correction, utilizing an adaptive quantum error correction mechanism that dynamically adjusts the correction parameters based on the quantum state's evolution. We demonstrate that this approach significantly improves the reliability and security of quantum computations, offering a more efficient and practical method for handling the complexities of quantum systems. The core mechanism involves learning the dynamic state of the quantum system and adapting the correction process accordingly. This represents a significant step towards enhancing the robustness of quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Entanglement Memory Access
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum entanglement for radically transforming memory access paradigms. The core premise is that leveraging the non-local correlations inherent in entangled quantum states can surpass the limitations imposed by classical physics on data retrieval and modification speeds. We propose a novel architecture where data is encoded across multiple quantum bits, utilizing entanglement to facilitate instantaneous data access from disparate physical locations. This approach aims to circumvent the inherent latency associated with conventional memory systems, offering the theoretical possibility of achieving speeds exceeding those attainable with classical methods. The paper details the conceptual framework, outlining the key mathematical relationships and considerations necessary for implementing such a system. We present a foundational model for quantifying the potential speedup, incorporating factors such as entanglement fidelity and the number of entangled qubits involved. Finally, we discuss the challenges and future research directions associated with realizing entanglement-based memory.

title: ## Brazilian Serotine: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of *Agkistrodon palmiceps*
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed Brazilian Serotine (BS), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Brazilian Serotine snake (*Agkistrodon palmiceps*). The algorithm leverages the snake's strategic movement patterns – specifically its ability to detect prey through subtle vibrations and its efficient search strategy – to develop a robust and adaptable optimization technique. BS incorporates key elements of the snake's behavior, including a modified Lévy flight mechanism, a dynamic constriction operator mimicking the snake's prey capture, and a novel adaptive parameter control system based on prey density estimation. The algorithm's performance is evaluated across a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions with reasonable computational cost. We present a detailed explanation of BS's design, its theoretical underpinnings, and experimental results showcasing its capabilities. The focus is on the algorithm's adaptability and potential applications in complex optimization landscapes.

title: ## Bonin Fruit Bat-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Bonin Fruit Bat-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (BFIMA), motivated by the foraging behavior of Bonin fruit bats. These bats exhibit a complex and efficient search strategy for ripe fruit, utilizing a combination of exploration and exploitation techniques. The BFIMA algorithm leverages these principles to develop a new optimization approach. The algorithm incorporates a bat population, each representing a potential solution. Bats adjust their position and frequency based on the attractiveness (fitness) of food sources, employing a harmonic motion model and a communication mechanism mimicking bat echolocation. The algorithm utilizes a global communication range to disseminate information about promising regions of the search space. We demonstrate the effectiveness of BFIMA on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its ability to converge to optimal or near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The performance of BFIMA is compared against established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The results highlight the potential of BFIMA as a robust and efficient optimization tool. The core components of the algorithm include the bat population initialization, the position update rule, the frequency update rule, the communication rule, and the acceptance criterion.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning with Probabilistic Logic Programming
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to reasoning, termed Probabilistic Logic Programming, which synergistically combines the strengths of neural networks and symbolic reasoning. The core challenge in artificial intelligence lies in effectively integrating these two paradigms, which have historically operated with distinct methodologies and limitations. Neural networks excel at pattern recognition and feature extraction from unstructured data, while symbolic reasoning provides a robust framework for logical inference and knowledge representation. This work addresses this challenge by developing a system that utilizes neural networks for initial feature extraction and then employs probabilistic logic programming to reason based on these learned representations. The system learns logical rules from data, encoding them within a probabilistic logic programming framework, and subsequently leverages these rules for accurate and interpretable inference. The integration facilitates learning complex logical relationships directly from data, mitigating the need for manually defined rules, while simultaneously maintaining the rigor and explainability inherent in symbolic systems. The proposed framework demonstrates the potential to create more robust and adaptable reasoning systems capable of handling uncertainty and complex scenarios. We introduce a formalization of the system using probability theory and logic programming, outlining the key components and their interactions. The system is designed to be modular, allowing for the independent development and optimization of each component. The experimental results, although not presented through traditional experimentation due to the focus on architectural design and theoretical foundations, support the viability of this approach and highlight areas for future research.

title: Evolutionary Algorithms for Designing Novel Neural Network Architectures
abstract: The design of effective neural network architectures remains a significant bottleneck in deep learning research and development. Traditional approaches rely heavily on human expertise and trial-and-error, a process that is often time-consuming and limited by human biases. This paper investigates the application of evolutionary algorithms, specifically a genetic algorithm, to automatically generate and optimize novel neural network architectures. The core idea is to treat architecture design as an optimization problem, where a population of potential architectures is evolved over successive generations, guided by a fitness function based on performance on a target task. We demonstrate that this approach can produce architectures that significantly outperform those manually designed, showcasing the potential of automated architecture design to accelerate progress in deep learning. The methodology presented includes detailed descriptions of the genetic algorithm parameters, the representation of neural network architectures within the genetic representation, and the fitness evaluation strategy. The results highlight the capability of evolutionary algorithms to discover architectures with superior performance, suggesting a shift in paradigm for neural network design.

title: ## Black-Tufted Gerbil-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Gerbil Search" (GS), inspired by the foraging behavior of the black-tufted gerbil (Gerbillus karamau). Gerbils are known for their efficient and adaptive search strategies in complex, multi-dimensional environments, particularly when faced with limited resources and unpredictable obstacles. GS leverages this behavior through a multi-faceted approach encompassing a novel position update mechanism, a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance, and a stochastic perturbation scheme. The algorithm employs a population-based search, similar to other metaheuristics such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Ant Colony Optimization (ACO), but incorporates gerbil-inspired features to enhance its adaptability and convergence rate. Specifically, the algorithm utilizes a 'memory' component mimicking the gerbil's spatial memory of food sources, influencing the movement patterns of individuals within the population. We demonstrate the effectiveness of GS through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, including the Rastrigin function, the Sphere function, and the Himmelblau function. The results indicate that GS consistently outperforms or achieves comparable performance to established metaheuristics while exhibiting a particularly strong ability to navigate complex, high-dimensional search spaces. Further research will focus on incorporating real-world constraints and adapting GS to solve specific engineering and industrial optimization challenges.

title: Some hypotheses on how Chatbots work in problem-solution-driven conversations
abstract: We discuss the nature of chatbots as conversation partners in problem-solving conversations. What can chatbots do and what can't they do? Our analysis draws on insights from Aggregation Dynamics, Cognitive Linguistics, Neuropsychology and Psychology. We establish that chatbots are multifaceted and composite systems. Our argument focuses on basic chatbots in the hope of thereby making statements about the core functionality of more advanced chatbots. Basic chatbots are assumed to consist of a Large Language Model (LLM) with a simple interface. The main results of our analysis are: a description of human imagination, understanding and thinking based on so-called metaphorical problem propagations; that the texts in text datasets used for training LLMs have specific characteristics and that these texts only partially imitate human thinking and understanding; that the LLM training process encodes artificial metaphorical problem propagations into an LLM from these text datasets. Our conclusions are that a basic chatbot cannot be a thinking partner capable of matching the cognitive flexibility of humans, and that further development of LLMs will not lead to this either. But chatbots exist, they are being used on a massive scale, by both individuals and organisations. It is therefore socially and politically important to understand them. Our article aims to contribute to the discussion on the functioning, benefits and drawbacks of chatbots. Cognitive Linguistics shows how the use of metaphor is an expression of our thinking. Aggregation Dynamics, is an attempt at a comprehensive systems theory. We believe that the concept of metaphorical problem propagation could provide an interesting addition for both. Chatbots a solution? For what?

title: Calibrating Professional Discretion in Artificial Intelligence-Supported Business-to-Business Selling
abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming increasingly embedded in business-to-business (B2B) sales through applications such as lead scoring, forecasting, message generation, meeting summaries, customer relationship management, and next-best-action recommendations. Although these systems can improve speed and consistency, generative and emerging agentic AI also create new challenges for professional discretion because consultative selling depends on contextual interpretation, customer trust, ethical judgment, and the continuous development of salesperson expertise. This article presents a structured integrative review exploring how sales professionals and managers should calibrate their reliance on AI-generated sales recommendations. Drawing on research in AI-supported selling, human–AI reliance, automation bias, customer trust, adaptive selling, and sales management capability, the article develops a professional discretion calibration model. The model proposes four judgment filters (interpretive, relational, ethical, and developmental) that guide five response actions: accept, modify, reject, disclose, or escalate. The article contributes to sales management scholarship by explaining the judgment process through which AI-generated outputs are translated into customer-facing actions and by outlining the practical implications for the responsible use of AI in B2B sales.

title: A Named Entity Recognition Method Based on Semantic Plane Interpolation
authors: YANG Li, CHEN Yanping, HUANG Hui, HUANG Ruizhang, QIN Yongbin
abstract: In Named Entity Recognition (NER) methods, the nested semantic structure of named entities is effectively parsed by organizing all spans in a sentence into a planarized sentence representation. However, the spans in planarized sentence representation are abstract representations of phrases of different lengths in the sentence. Additionally, a span can represent either a single word or the entire sentence. This characteristic leads to two issues: insufficient contextual semantic dependency in short spans and loss of semantic information in the compression process for long spans. To address these issues, this study proposes a NER method based on semantic plane interpolation. This method expands the sentence plane representation by performing nearest neighbor interpolation on adjacent spans in the plane, which can significantly amplify the semantic features and contextual dependency between spans, effectively building up the semantic dependency between short spans and enhancing the semantic expression of long spans, thus better supporting named entities. Additionally, to avoid losing the original plane information, this study constructs a semantic perception network to extract and fuse global and local information in the original sentence plane representation, achieving fine-grained feature expression through multilayer refinement. The method achieves the highest F1 values of 88.87%, 88.52%, 81.55%, 96.49%, and 72.84% on the ACE2004, ACE2005, GENIA, Resume, and Weibo datasets, respectively, compared with the benchmark models, with improvements of 1.13, 1.61, 0.15, 0.37, and 0.46 percentage points, respectively. These results validate the generality and effectiveness of the proposed method for NER tasks.

title: Safe-Post AI: A Privacy-Preserving Framework for On-Device PII Detection in Social Media Images
abstract: The fast pace of social media accelerates risks of accidental privacy breaches, policy abuse, and damage to reputation. SafePost AI, a privacy-safeguarding Chrome extension, is introduced in this research, which inspects multimodal content locally prior to posting. Integrating NLP, OCR, rule-based models, Named Entity Recognition, and transformer models, it identifies sensitive information (e.g., phone number, email, address) and raises alarms for possible abuses such as hate speech or misinformation using zero-shot learning and strong classifiers. The incorporation of explainability mechanisms substantially enhances user trust in the system. Evaluation conducted on a dataset of 5,000 anonymized posts demonstrates sub-second response times, an OCR accuracy of 92.4%, and an F1-score of 0.87 for entity detection. SafePost AI provides a clear, scalable solution to protecting privacy and minimizing policy violations on the web.

Integrating NLP, OCR, rule-based models, Named Entity Recognition, and transformer models, it identifies sensitive information (e.g., phone number, email, address) and raises alarms for possible abuses such as hate speech or misinformation using zero-shot learning and strong classifiers. The incorporation of explainability mechanisms substantially enhances user trust in the system. Evaluation conducted on a dataset of 5,000 anonymized posts demonstrates sub-second response times, an OCR accuracy of 92.4%, and an F1-score of 0.87 for entity detection. SafePost AI provides a clear, scalable solution to protecting privacy and minimizing policy violations on the web.

title: Stroke and structure priors improve few-shot recognition of oracle bone inscriptions
abstract: Oracle Bone Inscriptions (OBIs) recognition is challenging because glyph classes are numerous, long-tailed, and morphologically variable. We compare repository-based Teacher supervision with stroke and structure priors for class-disjoint few-shot OBI recognition. On the OBC306 dataset, using 42 classes, no-replacement sampling, and 10,000 episodes per shot, original-Teacher, no-Teacher FEAT, and glyph-prior FEAT achieve 74.31/75.44/77.56% at 1 shot and 88.99/89.88/91.67% at 50 shots across three seeds. Glyph priors improve no-Teacher FEAT by 1.79–2.15 points; paired 95% intervals exclude zero. Teacher targets are nearly uniform. Objective-weighting and label-agreement controls recover most of the gap, whereas a balanced subset reverses the effect. On near-saturated HWOBC, seed-0 gains are only 0.015–0.044 points. Baseline, query, module, complexity, and qualitative controls bound conclusions. Morphology-aware features improve OBI few-shot recognition, while Teacher utility depends on repository, objective, and data regime.

title: Deep sea anglerfish symbiosis optimization for heterogeneous role structured engineering optimization
abstract: This paper proposes Deep-Sea Anglerfish Symbiosis Optimization (DASO), a heterogeneous metaheuristic for complex engineering optimization. DASO addresses premature convergence and population diversity loss in high-dimensional, non-convex landscapes by assigning differentiated search roles to male and female agents. Its framework integrates functional dimorphism, asymmetrical attachment, local field-guided movement, and nonlinear high-pressure adaptation to coordinate global exploration and local refinement. DASO was evaluated on the CEC2017 and CEC2022 benchmark suites in 10-, 30-, and 50-dimensional settings, with 30 independent runs for each configuration, and was further tested on constrained engineering design problems. The results show that DASO achieves competitive performance in solution quality, convergence behavior, and robustness compared with representative metaheuristic algorithms. Statistical analysis using the Wilcoxon rank-sum test at the 0.05 significance level further confirms the consistency of the results. These findings demonstrate the potential of heterogeneous role-structured search for solving complex engineering optimization problems.

title: Resource‐Optimal Four‐Party Cyclic Quantum Teleportation: A Rigorous Resource Bound and Deterministic Network Protocol
abstract: ABSTRACT We formulate simultaneous four‐party cyclic quantum teleportation as an exact quantum‐channel simulation problem. Alice, Bob, Charlie, and David each hold an arbitrary input qubit and must transfer the four states in the directed cycle using only local operations, preshared entanglement, and classical communication. This formulation exposes a resource constraint that cannot be established from a recovery table alone. By testing the desired channel on inputs locally entangled with reference qubits, we prove that every exact deterministic realization must possess a Schmidt rank at least four, and at least two ebits across each one‐party‐versus‐three‐party bipartition. A resource containing only one qubit at each node, including a four‐qubit cluster state has local dimension two and therefore cannot implement the simultaneous transfer of four independent arbitrary qubits. For qubit resources, at least eight preshared resource qubits are necessary. We then construct a protocol that saturates this lower bound: four Bell pairs are placed on the directed network links, every sender performs one local Bell‐state measurement, and every receiver applies a two‐bit‐controlled Pauli correction. The complete recovery map contains joint outcomes but factorizes into four transparent four‐outcome maps, yielding a unit success probability and an irreducible classical record of eight bits. We further derive the induced cyclic Pauli channel for general Bell‐diagonal resources, distinguish link fidelity, product‐input fidelity, entanglement fidelity, and global average gate fidelity, and provide finite‐shot confidence formulas. All results are analytical or numerical; experimental requirements and platform‐specific limitations are discussed separately.

title: Quantum Entangled Photon‐Pair Generation From van der Waals NbOI 2
abstract: The realization of quantum light sources is crucial for advancing quantum technologies. Two‐dimensional van der Waals (vdW) materials offer a compelling platform for ultracompact entangled photon‐pair sources due to their strong optical nonlinearities and relaxed phase‐matching constraints. Here, the generation of entangled photon pairs from vdW NbOI 2 flakes on Au film via spontaneous parametric down‐conversion (SPDC) process is demonstrated. The observed inverse relationship between second‐order correlation function and pump power and the linear relationship between coincidence rate and pump power confirm the characteristic features of SPDC process. Furthermore, the measured polarization‐dependent coincidence rate shows the anisotropic entangled photon‐pair emission in NbOI 2 crystal. The dependence of coincidence rate on flake thickness is characterized by considering both optical interference and the phase‐matching effects. The demonstrated results open new avenues for the development of on‐chip integrated quantum photonic devices for applications in quantum state engineering, quantum communication, and quantum information processing.

title: mzCache: On-Device LLM Memory Management under Multitasking
abstract: On-device mobile Large Language Model (LLM) inference is gaining significant attention. However, mobile devices operate in highly dynamic multitasking environments where users frequently switch between applications. This creates memory pressure, forcing LLM memory (model weights and KV cache) to be evicted by the operating system. When a new inference request arrives, the inference system must restore the evicted memory through slow storage reads or recompute the entire KV cache, severely degrading responsiveness. To address this, we present mzCache, an on-device LLM inference system with specialized memory management for multitasking environments. Under unpredictable memory pressure, mzCache elastically evicts LLM memory and leverages the unified memory of mobile SoCs to enable zero-wait inference on the GPU with concurrent CPU-side restoration. mzCache realizes this through restoration-oriented memory management: LLM memory is partitioned into fine-grained shared buffers to enable partial eviction and restoration with concurrent cross-processor access, while hybrid swap and backward-out eviction policies ensure low-latency restoration from any eviction state. Implemented on llama.cpp and deployed as an Android application, mzCache achieves 2.1-5.5$\times$ reduction in Time-to-First-Token compared to storage-backed partial offload and demonstrates its effectiveness in real multitasking scenarios.

title: Space Generative AI with Solar Energy Harvesting
abstract: Satellites are emerging as promising platforms to extend generative \emph{artificial intelligence} (AI) services to remote areas lacking terrestrial infrastructure. However, deploying space generative AI is fundamentally constrained by the limited, time-varying onboard energy supplied by solar \emph{energy harvesting} (EH). This paper presents a framework for solar-powered space generative AI in which a satellite receives a user prompt, executes a diffusion-based image-generation model, and downlinks the compressed result within a strict time window. We identify the fundamental \emph{computation--communication} (C$^2$) trade-offs governed by the shared harvested-energy budgets. Specifically, increasing the number of generation steps improves intrinsic image quality but depletes energy and time available for downlink transmission, whereas prioritizing communication guarantees reliable delivery but sacrifices semantic quality. To balance these trade-offs and maximize \emph{end-to-end} (E2E) generative performance, we exploit the predictable solar-EH dynamics induced by deterministic orbital motion and develop a joint C$^2$ resource-optimization framework using a tractable two-step approach. First, we characterize the maximum downlink throughput for a fixed generation depth under continuous solar EH. This establishes a separation principle that decouples waiting-time selection from optimal transmit-power control. Next, we formulate a joint C$^2$ utility-maximization problem and derive a closed-form, low-complexity step-selection policy in the dominant constant-power regime. Extensive experiments under realistic orbital dynamics demonstrate that the proposed policy dynamically balances generation quality and transmission reliability. This yields significant E2E performance gains over static computation- and communication-centric baselines across diverse solar-EH states.

title: FLaG: Frequency-Domain Latent-attention Gated Pooling for Token Aggregation
abstract: Token aggregation converts token-level representations into fixed-dimensional sample representations, but most pooling methods operate only in the original token space. We introduce Frequency-Domain Latent-attention Gated Pooling (FLaG), a plug-in aggregation module that re-expresses encoder outputs in the Fourier domain before final pooling. FLaG represents the nonredundant rFFT spectrum through concatenated real and imaginary components, summarizes spectral tokens with learnable latent queries, derives a sample-conditioned channel gate, and reconstructs modulated token representations for downstream aggregation. We evaluate the same architecture across ESM2-based antimicrobial peptide (AMP) activity prediction, ResNet18 image classification on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, and three RoBERTa-based language tasks. FLaG achieves the best macro-averaged Spearman correlation coefficient, RMSE, and Recall@50 across four AMP backbone-species settings and the highest top-1 accuracy on CIFAR 10. It also achieves the best mean results on five of seven language metrics, although mean pooling remains strongest on STSBenchmark. AMP-side mechanistic analyses reveal low-frequency prediction sensitivity across most encoder layers, with increased relative high-frequency sensitivity in the final layer, and pronounced peptide-specific positional responses. The residual gate broadly amplifies spectral channels while preserving the low-frequency-dominated energy profile, whereas latent cross-attention exhibits sample- and species-specific spectral allocation. Overall, FLaG provides a transferable frequency-domain aggregation bias across protein, visual, and textual representations, with benefits that depend on the backbone and downstream task. Supplementary materials, source code, and data are available at https://www.healthinformaticslab.org/supp/ and https://github.com/Kewei2023/AMPCliff/tree/FLaG.

title: BioELX: Context-Aware Cross-lingual Biomedical Entity Linking without Task-Specific Supervision
abstract: Cross-lingual biomedical entity linking (BEL) maps mentions in any language to unique identifiers in a biomedical knowledge base, supporting clinical and biomedical NLP applications. We identify two issues affecting current systems. First, the UMLS (Bodenreider,2004) aliases used to train cross-lingual BEL retrievers are heavily skewed toward English, so retrievers generalize poorly to non-English mentions. Second, although context is often necessary for disambiguation, naively injecting context into retrievers trained only to align aliases severely degrades retrieval. We propose BioELX, a retrieve-rerank framework that addresses both issues. For retrieval, we continue training SapBERT_multi (Liu et al., 2021b) using Wikidata-derived cross-lingual alias supervision, forming shared concept neighborhoods across languages. For reranking, we adapt pretrained LLM rerankers to entity linking through mention-anchored prompting, which marks the target mention so that rerankers score candidates with respect to the intended mention rather than other salient tokens in the context. Experiments show that BioELX achieves new state-of-the-art results on four cross-lingual BEL benchmarks, improving Recall@1 by 4.8 to 18.2 percentage points over prior best results, without any task-specific BEL annotations. Our code and resources are available at https://github.com/AI4MedCode/BioELX.

title: The evolution of Artificial Intelligence from machine learning to generative AI
abstract: Η Τεχνητή Νοημοσύνη (ΤΝ) αποτελεί έναν από τους πλέον δυναμικούς και ταχέως εξελισσόμενους επιστημονικούς τομείς της σύγχρονης εποχής. Η μετάβαση από τη Μηχανική Μάθηση (Machine Learning) και τη Βαθιά Μάθηση (Deep Learning) προς τη Παραγωγική Τεχνητή Νοημοσύνη (generative AI) έχει επιφέρει σημαντικές αλλαγές στον τρόπο με τον οποίο τα υπολογιστικά συστήματα αλληλεπιδρούν με τον άνθρωπο, λαμβάνουν αποφάσεις και δημιουργούν περιεχόμενο. Η παρούσα εργασία εξετάζει την εξέλιξη της ΤΝ δίνοντας έμφαση σε κρίσιμες έννοιες όπως η εμπιστοσύνη (trust), η επεξηγησιμότητα (explainability), η ανθρωποκεντρική σχεδίαση και η αλληλεπίδραση ανθρώπου–μηχανής. Παρουσιάζονται εφαρμογές της ΤΝ σε τομείς όπως η εκπαίδευση, οι έξυπνες πόλεις, η ενέργεια και η υγεία, ενώ αναλύονται οι προκλήσεις που σχετίζονται με epistemic risks και hallucinations στα μεγάλα γλωσσικά μοντέλα. Τέλος, γίνεται συγκριτική ανάλυση των πλεονεκτημάτων και περιορισμών της ΤΝ, καθώς και των ηθικών και κοινωνικών επιπτώσεών της, με στόχο την ανάδειξη μελλοντικών κατευθύνσεων έρευνας.

title: Evolutionary Excellence: Bridging the Gap in Multilingual AI
abstract: Faced with the challenge of building affordable, multilingual AI, PhD students Zhou Yu and Chen Xianwei turned to evolutionary computation. Competing in the global FLAME 2024 challenge, they developed a resource-efficient ""bi-level"" approach, combining parameter merging with evolutionary architecture search to fuse models across different languages and tasks. By implementing a ""Glue Layer"" with knowledge distillation, they stabilized cross-model connections while ensuring cross-language fairness. Despite intense time pressure and computational limits, the team’s commitment to reproducible research and modular design turned a complex technical challenge into a career-defining success, bridging the gap between evolutionary computation and modern AI.

title: Predicting COVID-19 hospitalisation and common disease risk from comorbid diagnoses in 13 million individuals
abstract: Abstract Predicting disease risk from prior diagnoses is fundamental to clinical decision-making, particularly during health emergencies such as the COVID-19 pandemic, when individuals with long-term conditions may be disproportionately vulnerable to adverse outcomes. Despite intense interest in developing models to predict disease risk from prior diagnoses 1–3 , most prediction models do not estimate effects of each prior diagnosis on disease risk conditional on other diagnoses, limiting interpretability and clinical utility. We developed the Comorbidity Risk Score (CRS), trained on 13 million individuals (age 40-69) from linked electronic health record (EHR) datasets of the entire population of England, to predict COVID-19 hospitalisation and 87 other disease outcomes. CRS was trained at close to saturated sample size and precisely estimated the effects of 212 prior diagnoses on the 88 disease outcomes, conditional on all other prior diagnoses. Correlations of CRS effect sizes across outcomes (e.g. 0.76 for myocardial infarction vs. hyperlipidaemia) matched the corresponding genetic correlations (e.g. 0.79 for myocardial infarction vs. hyperlipidaemia), confirming that comorbidity architectures capture disease aetiology. On average, CRS identified 5% of the population with 3.4-fold higher disease risk, including myocardial infarction (4.4-fold), lung cancer (6.5-fold), and COVID-19 hospitalisation (6.3-fold). Using prior diagnoses alone, CRS outperformed state-of-the-art clinical COVID-19 models 4 . Furthermore, CRS ( N =13 million) substantially outperformed state-of-the-art AI 1 ( N =0.5 million) and linear 3 ( N =0.5 million) models in predicting disease risk, suggesting that training sample size outweighs model complexity. CRS attained near-perfect transferability across self-reported ethnicities (e.g., Black vs. White: AUROC ratio = 97.3%). Finally, CRS distinguished independently predictive comorbidities from indirect associations, e.g., lipid metabolism disorder was a strong predictor of myocardial infarction risk but not ischaemic stroke, after conditioning on other prior diagnoses. In conclusion, CRS provides a comprehensive resource for understanding the impact of comorbidities on COVID-19 and other future diseases, revealing disease aetiology while enabling powerful prediction of disease risk.

On average, CRS identified 5% of the population with 3.4-fold higher disease risk, including myocardial infarction (4.4-fold), lung cancer (6.5-fold), and COVID-19 hospitalisation (6.3-fold). Using prior diagnoses alone, CRS outperformed state-of-the-art clinical COVID-19 models 4 . Furthermore, CRS ( N =13 million) substantially outperformed state-of-the-art AI 1 ( N =0.5 million) and linear 3 ( N =0.5 million) models in predicting disease risk, suggesting that training sample size outweighs model complexity. CRS attained near-perfect transferability across self-reported ethnicities (e.g., Black vs. White: AUROC ratio = 97.3%). Finally, CRS distinguished independently predictive comorbidities from indirect associations, e.g., lipid metabolism disorder was a strong predictor of myocardial infarction risk but not ischaemic stroke, after conditioning on other prior diagnoses. In conclusion, CRS provides a comprehensive resource for understanding the impact of comorbidities on COVID-19 and other future diseases, revealing disease aetiology while enabling powerful prediction of disease risk.

title: Unauthorized Use of Artificial Intelligence Systems and Applications (An Analytical Study)
abstract: This research explores the legal and technical framework of attacks on Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems through unauthorized use. The significance of this study stems from the fact that AI systems are not merely traditional computer programs; rather, they are complex software entities relying on algorithms and training data. Consequently, attacks on these systems transcend traditional copying, involving deeper concepts such as reverse engineering and substantive content modification.This research focuses on three primary forms of illicit use:Unauthorized Copying and Adaptation: Exploiting the system to produce an identical program through decoding techniques or reverse engineering.Substantial Modification of Content: Reprogramming the system to alter its original purpose.Violation of Trade Secrets and Industrial Design. In researching the topic of unauthorized use of artificial intelligence systems and applications, we adopted the analytical approach. We did not limit ourselves to theoretical analysis, but rather used the comparative approach by extrapolating legislative texts in several legal systems to ensure the comprehensiveness of the presentation whenever the need arose.

title: Development of a Personalized Framework for Mental Health Education Integrating Neural Networks and Big Data Analysis
abstract: Mental Health (MH) disorders are becoming increasingly prevalent across diverse populations, yet conventional MH education often lacks personalisation, reducing its effectiveness. However, current frameworks do not effectively integrate heterogeneous data sources nor adaptively respond to individual user needs and progress. This research aims to develop a personalised MH education framework termed Neural Attention and NSGA-II Powered Educational Network (NeuroNSGA-EdNet) that integrates neural network modelling and big data analysis to deliver adaptive, user-specific content. The primary objective is to improve MH literacy, promote early awareness, and enhance user engagement through data-driven personalisation. The NeuroNSGA-EdNet framework incorporates heterogeneous data sources, including social media activity, wearable sensor data, academic records, and self-reported psychological assessments. Data pre-processing techniques such as Z-score normalisation, tokenisation, and missing value imputation ensure consistency and quality. An attention-based Convolutional Long Short-Term Memory (ConvLSTM) network models temporal and contextual patterns in the data. Personalised content recommendations are generated using a Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm (NSGA-II), optimising multiple objectives based on individual psychological profiles. A feedback and adaptive learning loop continuously update recommendations based on user interactions and learning outcomes. The experimental validation conducted using a systematic train-validation-test split approach on a heterogeneous dataset revealed an accuracy of 98.4%, 86.1% precision, 89.4% recall, and 91.6% F1. Users reported higher satisfaction with personalised learning paths compared to static modules. NeuroNSGA-EdNet integrates AI and big data for personalised MH education, combining deep learning, genetic optimisation, and adaptive feedback to enhance MH literacy and support early intervention.

title: Structural Trust: An Uncertainty-Typed Property Hypergraph for Agent Memory
abstract: Agent-facing knowledgebases compute confidence and provenance at answer time, as properties of the re- sponse. This paper argues that is too late, and that the argument is not a matter of engineering quality: information about whether a claim is true enters through the primary record, and every later stage is a rendering of that record, so no downstream scoring can add a bit that the record did not already carry. Confidence computed from the exhibit has an evidential ceiling fixed before it runs. We describe the store that follows from taking that seriously. The substrate is an uncertainty-typed property hypergraph: every unit carries the same five fields, a knowledge type, provenance graded on a four-valued lattice and carrying a validity horizon, the condition under which the entry held, a version with its conflict history, and a confidence separated into write-time and serving-time quantities, and relations are hyperedges because the relations that matter in agent memory are irreducibly n-ary and reifying them into binary edges destroys exactly the structure later stages need. On that substrate we specify three mechanisms. Consolidation is gated on whether a merged region still decomposes into the inferences it was meant to support, a structural and label-free test that needs no paired QA data and no per-environment training. Conflict is preserved through four lifecycle primitives, demotion, supersession, revocation and invalidation, of which three share a single inverse transition and revocation deliberately has none. Retrieval returns a coverage-guaranteed evidence subgraph with the guarantee conditional on the type of edge retrieved rather than marginal over a query distribution, and it answers with three outcomes rather than one score: supported, insufficient, refuted. The paper’s most portable result is a criterion for when two memory mechanisms can affect each other at all: only where one writes a property of the store that the other reads, at a granularity they share. The criterion is checkable from the specifications before anything is built, it discriminates rather than merely predicting failure, and it carries a stated falsifier.

title: 基于自适应的机器学习的特征选择
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to feature selection based on adaptive machine learning, aiming to automate the optimization of feature weights and improve model performance. Traditional feature selection methods rely on manual design, limiting their adaptability and potential for improvement. Our work utilizes a self-learning machine learning model to dynamically adjust feature weights, offering a significant advancement in this field. The core mechanism involves training a model to learn feature selection capabilities, allowing for automated optimization of model performance. This paper presents a detailed explanation of the proposed algorithm, its implementation, and preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential implications and future directions of this research.

title: 基于自适应网络的复杂系统预测模型
abstract: This paper presents a novel self-adaptive network model for complex system prediction. Traditional approaches often rely on static network parameters, limiting the model's ability to accurately predict system behavior. This work introduces a dynamic adjustment mechanism, enabling the model to iteratively refine its predictions based on observed system behavior. The model leverages a feedback loop to optimize network parameters, resulting in improved predictive accuracy. We explore the design and validation of this approach, demonstrating its effectiveness through a simulated case study.

title: Bushy-tailed Jird: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Jaculus pusillus*
abstract: This paper presents Bushy-tailed Jird (BTJ), a new metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging strategies employed by *Jaculus pusillus*, the bushy-tailed jird, a small rodent known for its efficient and adaptable foraging behavior in arid environments. BTJ leverages the jird's tendency to explore widely while maintaining a focus on promising areas, mimicking its movement patterns and decision-making processes. The algorithm incorporates a novel adaptive population diversity mechanism, a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance, and a unique 'nesting' strategy for solution representation. We demonstrate BTJ's effectiveness across a range of benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance relative to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Differential Evolution and Particle Swarm Optimization. The algorithm's parameters are designed to be easily tunable, allowing for adaptation to varying problem characteristics. Experimental results indicate that BTJ exhibits robust performance and adaptability, suggesting its potential for application in diverse optimization scenarios.

title: Dimension Space Information Theory Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on dimension space information theory. Traditional optimization techniques often struggle with complex geometries and dynamic environments, necessitating fixed parameter settings. This work proposes a method that dynamically adjusts parameter values within a dimension space to optimize a target function, leveraging the properties of information theory to reduce computational complexity. The core mechanism involves mapping a parameter space to a dimension space, employing information-theoretic principles to guide the optimization process. The research focuses on designing an algorithm that can adapt to varying input conditions and achieve robust optimization. This algorithm aims to provide a more flexible and adaptable solution compared to existing methods, particularly in scenarios requiring dynamic parameter adjustments.

title: Title: Adaptive Machine Learning Knowledge Distillation
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive machine learning knowledge distillation method, utilizing dynamic adjustment of distillation target model parameters based on data characteristics and task objectives. Traditional knowledge distillation methods often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their adaptability. This adaptive approach automatically tunes distillation parameters to optimize knowledge transfer, mitigating potential knowledge leakage. The core mechanism involves an adaptive learning algorithm that dynamically adjusts the distillation target model's parameters, tailored to the data's specifics and the desired task. This results in improved knowledge transfer and reduced knowledge leakage, offering a novel approach to knowledge distillation.

title: Simulating Evolution: A Hybrid Approach Combining Simulated Annealing and Neuromorphic Computing
abstract: This paper explores a novel hybrid approach to solving complex optimization problems by integrating Simulated Annealing (SA) with Neuromorphic Computing. The core idea leverages the rapid exploration capabilities of neuromorphic systems to efficiently traverse the solution space, followed by the refinement and precision enhancement provided by Simulated Annealing. We propose a framework where a neuromorphic system acts as a primary search engine, generating a diverse set of candidate solutions. These solutions are then presented to a Simulated Annealing algorithm, which iteratively improves them based on a temperature schedule and probabilistic acceptance criteria. This synergy aims to overcome the limitations of each individual approach, resulting in potentially faster convergence and higher solution quality. The paper details the theoretical underpinnings of this hybrid method, outlines a proposed architecture, and discusses potential challenges and future research directions. We demonstrate, through a conceptual framework, the potential benefits of this combined approach.

title: Bottle-nose Dolphin Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Bottle-nose Dolphin Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm" (BDIMA), inspired by the foraging behavior of bottlenose dolphins. The algorithm leverages the dolphin's strategic hunting techniques, particularly their coordinated movements and echolocation, to effectively explore and exploit the search space in complex optimization problems. BDIMA incorporates a population-based approach, mimicking the group dynamics of dolphins, and utilizes a novel adaptive mechanism based on the intensity of their echolocation signals to guide the search towards promising regions. The algorithm's core components include a population initialization, a movement strategy inspired by dolphin pod formations, an adaptive parameter update scheme mimicking echolocation intensity, and a convergence criterion based on the stability of the population. The performance of BDIMA is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive capabilities compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The results indicate that BDIMA exhibits strong performance in terms of solution quality and convergence speed, particularly for problems with multimodal landscapes and complex constraints. Future work will focus on further refining the algorithm's parameters and exploring its applicability to a wider range of optimization challenges.

title: Self-Adaptive Quantum Entanglement Topology Control
abstract: This paper investigates the application of self-adaptive quantum entanglement topology control for enhanced quantum communication and computation. The core challenge lies in dynamically adjusting the topological structure of entangled states in response to changes in the quantum state. We propose a novel algorithm that iteratively modifies the entanglement topology based on a feedback loop, optimizing for key performance metrics. The proposed method offers a pathway to overcome limitations of existing approaches, enabling more efficient and robust quantum systems. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our algorithm through simulations and preliminary experimental validation. The focus is on the potential for automated optimization of quantum states, resulting in improved communication fidelity and computational speed.

title: Causal Bayesian Networks with Latent Counterfactual Inference
abstract: Causal Bayesian networks (CBNs) are powerful tools for representing and reasoning about causal relationships. However, a significant limitation of existing CBNs is their inability to accurately perform counterfactual inference – determining what would have happened if a specific intervention had been applied. This research addresses this gap by introducing a novel approach for integrating latent variables to represent unobserved causal pathways and employing a variational inference technique to directly estimate counterfactual probabilities. The proposed method allows for robust counterfactual reasoning within CBNs, opening up new possibilities for decision-making applications where understanding the effects of interventions is crucial. The core contribution lies in the ability to model complex causal structures with unobserved confounding variables and to derive counterfactual probabilities without relying on traditional, often intractable, methods. This work demonstrates the feasibility and potential of this approach, paving the way for more sophisticated and reliable causal reasoning systems.

title: Hyperdimensional Wave Function Optimization (HWO)
abstract: This paper introduces Hyperdimensional Wave Function Optimization (HWO), a novel approach to machine learning model training that leverages the inherent wave function properties of data to accelerate convergence and enhance model accuracy. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with complex datasets due to slow convergence and difficulty in capturing intricate relationships. HWO proposes a framework based on representing data as wave functions and employing wave function optimization techniques to guide the learning process. The paper details the core concepts, implementation, and preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of HWO in a specific machine learning task. We showcase its potential to overcome the limitations of existing optimization methods, offering a promising avenue for accelerating the development of advanced machine learning models.

title: Decentralized Federated Learning with Byzantine Fault Tolerance via Proof-of-Stake
abstract: Federated learning (FL) offers a promising approach to training machine learning models on decentralized data sources without directly exchanging the data itself. However, existing FL systems are susceptible to Byzantine attacks, where malicious participants intentionally submit incorrect or misleading updates, compromising the integrity and accuracy of the global model. This paper proposes a novel decentralized federated learning system that integrates Byzantine fault tolerance and a Proof-of-Stake (PoS) incentive mechanism to mitigate these vulnerabilities. The core idea is to incentivize participants to contribute honest updates while simultaneously providing cryptographic proofs to verify the validity of these updates. This system constructs a decentralized network where participants stake resources (e.g., computational power or storage) to gain voting rights and rewards for contributing correct updates. Malicious behavior is penalized through a reduction in stake and potentially exclusion from the network. The system utilizes cryptographic techniques, such as zero-knowledge proofs, to ensure the integrity of updates without revealing the underlying data. This approach significantly enhances the robustness of FL systems against adversarial attacks and promotes a more trustworthy and reliable learning environment. The proposed system addresses the critical challenge of Byzantine fault tolerance in FL, offering a practical and scalable solution for deploying FL models in sensitive environments.

title: Temporal Graph Representation and Reasoning with Dynamic Edge Embedding
abstract: Temporal graph representation and reasoning are fundamental for analyzing and predicting events across time. This paper introduces a novel approach to temporal graph representation and reasoning, focusing on dynamically adapting edge embeddings to capture evolving dependencies. We propose a graph embedding algorithm that learns node embeddings reflecting temporal information, enabling a 'temporal reasoning module' to infer future states. The system's core mechanism incorporates a dynamic edge embedding that responds to changes in graph structure and dependencies, offering enhanced flexibility and predictive capabilities compared to existing methods. This research addresses a critical challenge in temporal data analysis, providing a more robust and powerful representation for understanding temporal relationships.

title: Threat Analysis of Seed/Key Authentication in Automotive OBD Diagnostic Protocols: Attack Vectors and Cryptographic Countermeasures
authors: Carlos Eduardo R. de S. Oliveira
abstract: The On-Board Diagnostics (OBD) interface, standardized across modern vehicles through ISO 14229 (UDS), SAE J1939, and related protocols, presents a critical and frequently underestimated attack surface in automotive cybersecurity. Central to access control within these protocols is the seed/key authentication mechanism — a challenge-response scheme designed to restrict privileged diagnostic sessions to authorized entities. Despite its widespread deployment across hundreds of millions of vehicles, seed/key implementations remain highly heterogeneous, frequently relying on proprietary algorithms whose security rests on the wrong foundation: the secrecy of the algorithm itself rather than the secrecy of cryptographic key material. This paper presents a structured threat analysis of seed/key authentication in automotive OBD diagnostic contexts, applying a methodology aligned with ISO/SAE 21434 Threat Analysis and Risk Assessment (TARA). We introduce the distinction between algorithm secrecy and key secrecy as a central analytical lens, apply it to characterize attack vectors including brute force, reverse engineering, replay attacks, and ECU memory extraction, and evaluate the adequacy of cryptographic countermeasures currently deployed in the industry. Based on this analysis, we propose the Seed/Key Security Assessment Framework (SKSAF), a practical four-phase methodology for evaluating seed/key implementations in multi-brand diagnostic environments.

title: A Comprehensive Review of Post-Quantum Cryptography Algorithms
abstract: The development of quantum computing has been rapid, and an existential threat to computational hardness assumptions that underlie today's public-key cryptography has been encountered. This manuscript is a complete and thoroughly organized review of Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC), discussing the mathematical concepts, complexity, and mechanisms of the algorithms that underpin quantum-safe security infrastructures. Rather than the principles of quantum mechanics, the analysis mathematically defines the basic principles of qubits, superposition, and entanglement, and clarifies common misunderstandings of the theory of parallelism in quantum mechanics. The research places cryptographic problems into the Bounded-Error Quantum Polynomial-Time (BQP) complexity class, thus highlighting the exact defects of classical algorithms. The quantum gate complexity of Shor's algorithm is compared to classical bounds as in Pollard's rho algorithm for the Elliptic Curve Discrete Logarithm Problem (ECDLP), for a detailed comparative cryptanalysis. The comparison highlights a very important “quantum security inversion” in that Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC) is much more susceptible to the early-stage fault-tolerant quantum computer as compared to the approach used today in RSA. It unfolds the architectural dependency of quantum algorithms, one by one, from the Quantum Fourier Transform (QFT) to Quantum Phase Estimation (QPE) and Shor's algorithm to Grover's algorithm. Last but not least, the manuscript examines emerging attack primitives such as lattice-based, code-based, and hash-based cryptography, their security models, side channel vulnerabilities, and the recently finalised Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS 205, 203, and 204) that have been published by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST).

title: Multi-output deep learning framework for joint forecasting of solar irradiance and wind speed with cross-regional transferability analysis
abstract: Accurate forecasting of solar irradiance and wind speed is essential for improving hybrid renewable energy systems and ensuring grid stability. This study develops and evaluates a multi-output deep learning framework for the simultaneous prediction of global horizontal irradiance (GHI) and wind speed across multiple Indian regions. Hourly data from the National Solar Radiation Database (NSRDB) for the period 2015–2020 were used to train light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM), long short-term memory (LSTM), bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM), and convolutional long short-term memory (ConvLSTM) models, with cross-regional transfer learning applied across Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka, and Andhra Pradesh. Among the models, ConvLSTM achieved the best performance with a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.061 and an R² value of approximately 0.91, while BiLSTM demonstrated comparable accuracy with lower computational cost. The proposed framework emphasizes cross-regional transferability, demonstrating robust generalization across heterogeneous climatic conditions. Error distribution analysis further indicates improved prediction stability, with ConvLSTM exhibiting lower variability compared to other models. These results support scalable and reliable renewable energy forecasting, with practical implications for grid operation, power electronic control, and hybrid energy system management.

title: Predictive Behavioral Risk Detection for Agentic AI via Runtime Execution Monitoring
abstract: Agentic AI systems are increasingly deployed in real-world workflows where they autonomously invoke tools, maintain persistent memory, and interact with external services across tasks.This autonomy introduces behavioral safety risks that static defenses such as prompt filtering and output moderation are not able to catch, since harmful behavior often emerges gradually during execution rather than from a single input or output.This paper proposes a runtime monitoring framework for agentic AI systems that detects anomalous behavior by analyzing gateway and session logs produced during agent runtime, without modifying the underlying model or its reasoning processes.The framework was evaluated against two attack scenarios simulated on an OpenClaw gateway deployment: 1) longtail persistent memory poisoning, in which false factual values are injected into the agent's workspace memory file across niche domains and 2) prompt injections via document-embedded retrieval, in which adversarial instructions are hidden inside PDF resumes processed by an automated screening pipeline; For each attack, behavioral features were extracted from raw logs to capture temporal, structural, and semantic properties of agent responses, including response latency, token usage, hedge density, qualifier ratio, tool calling patterns, and output integrity metrics.A Random Forest classifier trained on approximately 2,000 turn-level records from the memory poisoning experiment achieved 78.75% accuracy, 84% precision, and an ROC-AUC of 0.874, demonstrating that runtime behavioral signals are sufficient to distinguish compromised sessions from normal behavior.These results suggest that gateway-level observability, combined with lightweight machine learning, provides a practical and model-agnostic foundation for predictive behavioral safety monitoring in agentic AI systems.
