title: Knowledge-enhanced two-dimensional semantic representation for named entity recognition
abstract: Discriminative models based on two-dimensional (2D) semantic representations have proven effective in modeling entity boundaries and nested structures in Named Entity Recognition (NER). However, their performance is often limited by challenges such as insufficient semantic generalization and the lack of external knowledge integration, particularly when dealing with sparse or domain-shifted annotations. On the other hand, generative large language models (LLMs) exhibit rich world knowledge and advanced semantic reasoning abilities, but they lack explicit structural modeling capabilities for precise entity boundary detection. This complementary nature between the two paradigms motivates the integration of discriminative and generative approaches for more robust and accurate NER. In this paper, we introduce a Knowledge-Enhanced NER (KE) framework, which synergistically combines a discriminative 2D semantic representation model with a generative LLMs-based refinement module. The discriminative model first captures sentence-level structural semantics and generates preliminary entity predictions, ensuring accurate boundary detection and nested entity recognition. Subsequently, a semantic similarity retrieval mechanism selects relevant annotated examples, which, alongside the target sentence and initial predictions, are fed into the generative LLMs to incorporate external knowledge and refine entity type classification. This recall-and-refine process enables the generative model to complement the discriminative model by correcting misclassified entities and recovering low-frequency or unannotated entities. The KE framework effectively merges the structural precision of discriminative models with the semantic generalization of generative models, creating a balanced and robust NER pipeline. Extensive experiments on multiple public benchmark datasets demonstrate that KE consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, particularly in nested NER tasks. Analytical studies further validate the effectiveness of the knowledge-enhancement mechanism in improving model robustness and cross-domain generalization.

title: An Introduction to Stochastic Deep Learning
abstract: ABSTRACT Deep neural networks (DNNs) have achieved remarkable success in prediction, but their deterministic formulation makes many statistical inference tasks difficult. StoNet, short for stochastic neural network, addresses this limitation by reformulating a DNN as a probabilistic latent‐variable model, in which the outputs of selected hidden layers or units are treated as latent variables. The article describes the formulation of StoNet and its asymptotic equivalence to a conventional DNN, showing how StoNet can serve both as a deep learning model and as an analytical device for studying DNNs. It reviews training algorithms for StoNet and discusses its applications to statistical inference problems, including nonlinear sufficient dimension reduction, causal inference with observed and unobserved confounders, Granger‐causality learning for nonlinear time series, nonlinear variable selection, and prediction uncertainty quantification for large‐scale DNNs. The article also discusses two related architectures: kernel‐expanded StoNet and sublinearly structured DNNs, which can be viewed as structural or theoretical extensions of the StoNet framework. Under suitable architectural conditions, the former is immune to local traps in training and tends to outperform conventional DNNs in prediction; whereas the latter achieves feature‐learning consistency in over‐parameterized regimes when the training sample size is sufficiently large. Together, these developments show that StoNet broadens deep learning from prediction‐oriented function approximation to a richer framework for statistical inference.

title: Dyn-3D: Unveiling and Resolving Ego-Motion Ambiguity in Vision-Language Models
abstract: As Vision-Language Models (VLMs) tackle dynamic 3D spatial reasoning, ego-motion perception becomes essential to resolve monocular scale ambiguity. However, current models often overfit to smooth trajectory priors rather than genuinely understanding physical motion. Consequently, their spatial reasoning degrades severely under large displacements, a phenomenon we term Kinematic Collapse. This failure stems from spurious visual-motion correlations in natural videos and a lack of explicit physical supervision. To evaluate this, we introduce Dyn-3D, a benchmark using counterfactual 3D rendering to rigorously decouple visual changes from true kinematic properties. Furthermore, we propose the TempoVista framework, featuring the Kinematic-GSPO algorithm. By embedding metric physical ground truth into policy optimization, TempoVista explicitly grounds visual representations in 3D space. Experiments demonstrate that our approach significantly improves both motion estimation and robust spatial reasoning by utilizing camera dynamics as an effective geometric calibration signal.

title: CoMMET: A Psychologically Grounded Benchmark for Evaluating Theory of Mind in Multimodal LLMs
abstract: Theory of Mind (ToM)-the ability to reason about the mental states of oneself and others-is a cornerstone of human social intelligence. As Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) become ubiquitous in real-world applications, validating their capacity for this level of social reasoning is essential for effective and natural interactions. However, existing benchmarks for assessing ToM in MLLMs are limited; most rely solely on text inputs and focus narrowly on belief-related tasks. In this paper, we propose a new multimodal benchmark dataset, CoMMET, a comprehensive mental states and moral evaluation task inspired by the Theory of Mind Booklet Task. CoMMET expands the scope of evaluation by covering a broader range of mental states and introducing multi-turn testing. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first psychology-grounded benchmark to evaluate MLLMs across multiple mental states in a multimodal, open-ended, and multi-turn setting. Through a comprehensive assessment of MLLMs across different families and sizes, we analyze the strengths and limitations of current models and identify directions for future improvement.

title: On Multiple Extended Object Tracking with Coastal X-Band Radars for Maritime Surveillance
abstract: Maritime trade carries the bulk of global freight, and safety with the security and environmental protection in congested waters strongly depends on reliable situational awareness. Although AIS is the primary cooperative information source, it is vulnerable to GNSS jamming, spoofing as well as to deliberate manipulation, which motivates an independent validation with coastal X-band radar. High-resolution sensors resolve vessels into many detections per scan, so the problem becomes one of multiple extended object tracking (EOT), where kinematics and target extent must be estimated jointly under clutter and occlusion conditions. This talk presents the two dominant families for this task: probabilistic data-association trackers ((J)IPDA family) and random-finite-set methods (PHD/CPHD), and shows that both can be driven from a common Random Matrix Model-based modeling with Gaussian kinematics and an Inverse-Wishart extent. Radar detections are grouped by density-based clustering applied directly in the polar domain, which preserves the native radar geometry and removes the range dependence of the clustering scale. The talk addresses the tracker-side mathematics that the tracking on high-resolution clusters demand: a stabilized extension clutter penalty, a log-domain hypothesis-generation backbone and measurement-driven birth model. Results on labelled real-world radar data from a station located in the Baltic Sea are reported for near- and far-field regions and suggestions for future works are provided.

title: Josephsonin digitaalisen vaiheilmaisimen optimointi kalorimetrin mittasignaalin digitointia varten
abstract: Scientific efforts and financial investments in quantum computers have increased in recent years, with superconducting architectures as one of the most promising platforms. To reach the true potential of quantum computers, the current systems need to be significantly scaled up. Current methods of superconducting qubit readout require routing between room-temperature electronics and the qubit which is operated in cryogenic conditions. When systems that use this approach are scaled up, problems arise; the numerous cables required for the routing to room temperature electronics become even more problematic as the system size increases. This method also suffers from increased measurement feedback latency which is worsened further by the scale-up. A novel architecture of on-chip qubit readout that addresses both of these problems is proposed by the Quantum Computing and Devices (QCD) group. The proposition involves a sensitive calorimeter which measures the qubit state. This measurement manifests as a change in the calorimeter frequency which can be further sensed by a probe-signal and encoded into the phase value of the reflected signal. To analyse the qubit state and determine the next action, the signal is required to be transferred to a control unit which determines the feedback to other microwave components. This requires digitisation of the reflected phase value. The method of digitisation that is proposed in the architecture utilises the Josephson digital phase detector (JDPD) which is a superconducting quantum circuit device that is also placed on chip. The JDPD is able to effectively digitise the phase value of an input signal owing to its non-linear potential, the configuration of which can be switched on command. However, the power of the reflected signal is extremely low which negatively affects the sensitivity of the JDPD and leads to higher detection error. The aim of this thesis is to increase the sensitivity of the JDPD with respect to low-power signals. This is achieved by optimising the critical current of the two Josephson junctions present in the system as well as the inductance of the central inductor. Successful optimisation makes the device more compatible with the proposed calorimetric qubit readout. The optimisation is conducted by simulating the system in Quantum Toolbox in Python (QuTiP) and analysing the resulting detection error. Before optimisation, the theory behind the system is discussed, and key operators are derived to later justify the parameters and assumptions that are chosen when optimising. Based on the simulations, this thesis found a low detection error space forinductance and critical current. The parameter pairs within this space yield adetection error of ∼ 41% which is an improvement from the, essentially random, baseline of ∼ 48%. The system has many free param.

title: Prioritizing Post-Quantum Migration in Synthetic Cryptographic Inventories with Machine Learning and QUBO Optimization
abstract: Post-quantum cryptography migration requires prioritizing cryptographic assets under budget and dependency constraints. This paper presents a reproducible pipeline combining supervised learning, heuristics, MILP, and QUBO. The evaluation covers three synthetic inventories with 1,609 assets, 1,179 migration candidates, and 1,050 dependencies. Logistic regression was selected for system-grouped priority estimation. Linear MILP achieved the highest predicted priority, closely followed by the priority-to-cost greedy method, while dependency-aware methods produced more coherent portfolios. Adding dependencies to QUBO reduced mean mandatory violations from 10.963 to 7.859 and increased coherence from 0.344 to 0.479, with a small priority decrease. Under the adopted soft objective, soft-dependency MILP achieved the best trade-off and substantially lower runtime. These results show that explicit dependency modeling improves migration coherence and that QUBO provides a flexible representation of budget and dependency interactions.

title: General Concepts on The Integration of Corpus Linguistics and Artificial Intelligence
abstract: This article analyzes the processes of integration between corpus linguistics and artificial intelligence technologies. It examines the use of modern artificial intelligence capabilities, particularly machine learning and deep neural networks, at the stages of compiling, collecting, tagging, and annotating linguistic corpora. The aim of the research is to theoretically and practically substantiate the interconnection between corpus linguistics methodology and artificial intelligence algorithms, and to determine their place within modern computational linguistics.

title: Implementasi Kriptografi Algoritma Rivest Shamir Adleman (RSA) pada Pengamanan Pesan Suara
abstract: Voice message security has become increasingly important in digital communication due to the risk of unauthorized access and eavesdropping during data transmission. Ensuring the confidentiality of voice data requires effective cryptographic techniques capable of protecting information from unauthorized parties. This study aims to implement the RSA cryptographic algorithm to secure voice messages through encryption and decryption processes. The research employed a software development approach by designing and developing a Python-based desktop application integrated with the RSA algorithm. Voice messages were encrypted using a public key and subsequently restored using the corresponding private key. The effectiveness of the implementation was evaluated through functional testing and signal analysis using waveform and Mel-spectrogram visualizations to compare the original, encrypted, and decrypted voice signals. The results demonstrate that the RSA algorithm successfully transforms voice messages into encrypted data that cannot be interpreted without the appropriate private key. Furthermore, the decrypted voice messages closely match the original recordings, confirming the correctness of the decryption process. The waveform and Mel-spectrogram analyses also reveal significant differences between the original and encrypted signals, while the decrypted signals exhibit characteristics similar to the original voice data. These findings indicate that RSA can be effectively applied to enhance the confidentiality and security of voice messages in digital communication systems, making it a reliable solution for protecting sensitive voice information from unauthorized access.

title: Javier-FernandezCarabantes/PyMOSTA: PyMOSTA v.0.1
abstract: PyMOSTA PyMOSTA is an open-source Python package for estimating the Magnitude of Completeness (Mc) and analyzing its spatiotemporal variability from seismic catalogs, designed for use by both seismological observatories and researchers. PyMOSTA is organized into independent yet interoperable modules for: Magnitude of completeness estimation (catalog-based methods) Synthetic catalog methods Spatial mapping and regional Mc analysis Temporal Mc evolution and catalog stability assessment Graphical visualization and interactive mapping This is a permanent archive mirroring the active GitHub repository of PyMOSTA.

title: Attention Conservation in Transformers: Testing for Global Flow Invariants Across Softmax, Residual, and MLP Pathways
abstract: This paper investigates whether softmax normalization in Transformer attention corresponds to a global conservation law, or only a local probabilistic constraint. Self-attention guarantees that outgoing attention weights from each query sum to one, inviting comparison with conservation constraints in flow networks and electrical circuits. We distinguish local normalization from cross-layer conservation and formulate an empirically testable protocol across three progressively complete Transformer representations: attention-only propagation, attention with residual connections, and the full attention-residual-MLP block. We hypothesize that softmax normalization alone does not imply global conservation, because the residual stream accumulates additive contributions rather than redistributing a fixed quantity. Candidate flow quantities are defined (attention mass, activation-weighted flow, feature-specific flow), alongside a conservation profile metric and an intervention protocol (token ablation, head ablation, activation patching, residual perturbation). A worked numerical case study illustrates the protocol's sensitivity across the three architectural systems. The question is situated against attention rollout and attention flow (Abnar and Zuidema, 2020), Flowformer's explicitly imposed flow conservation (Wu et al., 2022), and the descriptive, non-conservation-claiming use of circuit language in mechanistic interpretability (Olah et al., 2020; Elhage et al., 2021). Conservation is treated throughout as an open empirical hypothesis rather than an assumed structural fact.

title: Quantum Noise-Based Security Proof for Distributed Computing
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to enhancing the security and privacy of distributed computing systems by leveraging the inherent properties of quantum noise. Traditional cryptographic methods often struggle against advanced attacks, particularly in the context of distributed environments where key management and security protocols are complex. Our proposed solution utilizes a distributed key generation scheme predicated on quantum noise, exploiting its random and unpredictable nature to create a robust defense against potential adversaries. The core concept involves generating keys through a process sensitive to quantum noise, rendering traditional cryptanalytic techniques ineffective. We demonstrate that by carefully controlling and utilizing noise, we can achieve a significantly higher level of security compared to conventional methods. This research offers a fundamentally new security mechanism for distributed computing, providing a promising avenue for future cryptographic advancements. ---

title: Camiari Leaf-eared Mouse Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Camiari Leaf-eared Mouse Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (CLIMA), inspired by the foraging behavior of *Cavia leafear*, commonly known as the Camiari leaf-eared mouse. These rodents are renowned for their efficient and adaptive foraging strategies in complex environments. CLIMA leverages key aspects of their behavior, including exploration, exploitation, and path-finding, to create a robust optimization algorithm. The algorithm incorporates elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA) with modifications to mimic the Camiari leaf-eared mouse's sensory perception and navigational skills. Specifically, the algorithm utilizes a 'sensory radius' to define the search space and a 'path adaptation' mechanism to dynamically adjust the step size based on environmental feedback. The performance of CLIMA is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and competitive ability compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as PSO and Differential Evolution. The results show that CLIMA exhibits superior performance in terms of convergence speed and solution quality for challenging optimization tasks. The algorithm's adaptability and efficient search strategy make it a promising tool for solving complex real-world optimization problems.

title: 基于自适应的机器学习算法的强化学习应用
abstract: This paper investigates the integration of reinforcement learning and adaptive machine learning algorithms to create a dynamically adjusting learning framework. Traditional reinforcement learning often necessitates manual parameter tuning, limiting its flexibility and potential for optimal performance. We propose a novel approach that dynamically adjusts model parameters and strategies through a self-adaptive learning framework. The core mechanism involves combining reinforcement learning and adaptive machine learning, leveraging a self-learning architecture to optimize model performance based on environmental feedback. This research aims to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of reinforcement learning through enhanced parameter and strategy adaptation. The paper presents a framework and demonstrates its effectiveness through a simulated environment, showcasing the benefits of this integrated approach.

title: Dynamic Matrix Probability Model
abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic model based on dynamic matrices, offering a framework for more accurate probability predictions and modeling in dynamic systems. The core idea is to dynamically update a matrix representation of probability based on incoming data, enabling a more flexible and responsive approach to probabilistic inference. We explore the benefits of this approach, focusing on its ability to handle complex data transformations and achieve improved predictive accuracy. This paper presents a detailed theoretical analysis and provides a practical implementation of the dynamic matrix model, demonstrating its effectiveness through illustrative examples.

title: ## Brazilian Funnel-eared Bat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Funnel-eared Bat Optimization Algorithm" (FBOA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Brazilian funnel-eared bat ( *Rhacophorus brevicornis*). The algorithm leverages the bat's unique echolocation and flight patterns to effectively explore and exploit the search space in complex optimization problems. Specifically, the algorithm incorporates parameters mimicking the bat's frequency, intensity, and flight direction, utilizing these as key components within a stochastic search process. Mathematical formulations defining the core components of FBOA, including the echo distance, flight angle determination, and population update rules, are presented. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through a series of benchmark problems, demonstrating its potential for achieving robust and efficient solutions across diverse optimization challenges. The algorithm's key characteristics and advantages are highlighted, suggesting its applicability to a wide range of real-world applications. The core concept is to emulate the bat's navigational strategies to guide the search process towards optimal solutions.

title: Brandt's Hamster: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of Hamsters
abstract: This paper introduces Brandt's Hamster, a novel metaheuristic algorithm designed to enhance the performance of optimization problems. The algorithm draws inspiration from the foraging behavior of hamsters, specifically their tendency to explore and exploit promising areas within their environment. Brandt's Hamster employs a multi-layered exploration-exploitation strategy, utilizing a 'hamster burrow' representation for the search space and a 'food source' indicator to guide the algorithm's progression. The core of the algorithm lies in a dynamically adjusted 'burrow depth' parameter, controlling the balance between exploration and exploitation. A 'social learning' component, mimicking hamster interactions, further refines the search process. Mathematical formulations are presented to detail the algorithm's key components, including the probability of movement, the burrow depth update rule, and the food source identification mechanism. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and adaptability. The results indicate that Brandt's Hamster consistently outperforms traditional metaheuristic methods such as Genetic Algorithms and Particle Swarm Optimization in terms of solution quality and convergence speed. Keywords: Metaheuristic, Optimization, Foraging, Simulation, Algorithm Design, Artificial Intelligence, Brandt's Hamster.

title: Bomi Mountain Vole Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Bomi Mountain Vole Algorithm" (BMVA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Bomi Mountain Vole ( *Microtus bominus*). This rodent's unique strategy of navigating complex, uneven terrain to locate food sources provides a valuable framework for designing an efficient optimization algorithm. BMVA leverages concepts such as path exploration, obstacle avoidance, and resource prioritization, mimicking the vole's adaptive movement patterns. The algorithm employs a population-based approach with a novel encoding scheme representing potential solutions as sequences of steps. The core of BMVA lies in a dynamic adaptation of step length and direction based on terrain "elevation" (representing problem difficulty), and the presence of "obstacles" (representing constraints). A convergence criterion is defined based on population diversity and solution improvement. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and potential for real-world applications. This research contributes a new metaheuristic approach with a biologically inspired mechanism, offering a potentially robust and adaptable solution for tackling complex optimization challenges.

title: Bolivian Pampas Cat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Pampas Cat Algorithm" (PCA), inspired by the hunting strategies of the Bolivian Pampas Cat. The algorithm leverages the cat's unique ability to adapt its search strategy based on prey movement and environmental conditions. PCA utilizes a hybrid approach combining elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA) to effectively navigate complex, multi-dimensional optimization landscapes. Specifically, the algorithm incorporates a 'patience' parameter mimicking the cat's cautious approach, alongside a dynamically adjusted exploration-exploitation balance. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through theoretical analysis and simulations on several benchmark problems, showcasing its performance compared to established metaheuristic methods. The key contributions of this work are the novel adaptive search mechanism and the potential for improved convergence rates in challenging optimization scenarios. The algorithm's core formulaic representation is as follows: `x_i(t+1) = x_i(t) + rand(0,1) * A * (x_best(t) - x_i(t)) + F * (x_global_best(t) - x_i(t))`, where `x_i(t)` represents the position of the *i*-th particle at time *t*, `rand(0,1)` is a uniformly distributed random number between 0 and 1, `A` is a weight factor, `x_best(t)` is the best position found by the *i*-th particle at time *t*, `x_global_best(t)` is the best position found by all particles at time *t*, and `F` is a fading factor. The algorithm's convergence rate is defined as `CR = (fitness_current - fitness_previous) / fitness_previous`. The algorithm's performance is evaluated using metrics such as solution accuracy, computational cost, and convergence speed.

title: ## Bokiboky: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Bokiboky Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Bokiboky, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the Bokiboky, a fictional animal known for its complex and adaptable search strategies. Bokiboky exhibits characteristics of both particle swarm optimization (PSO) and ant colony optimization (ACO), combined with a unique 'exploration-exploitation' dynamic based on observed Bokiboky movements. The algorithm utilizes a novel position update rule, a dynamically adjusted pheromone decay rate, and a 'Bokiboky Shift' mechanism to enhance exploration and exploit promising regions of the search space. We demonstrate Bokiboky's effectiveness on several benchmark optimization problems, including the Rosenbrock function, Rastrigin function, and the Sphere function, showcasing its ability to converge to near-optimal solutions with competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. evidence.abstract: This paper presents Bokiboky, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the Bokiboky, a fictional animal known for its complex and adaptable search strategies. Bokiboky exhibits characteristics of both particle swarm optimization (PSO) and ant colony optimization (ACO), combined with a unique 'exploration-exploitation' dynamic based on observed Bokiboky movements. The algorithm utilizes a novel position update rule, a dynamically adjusted pheromone decay rate, and a 'Bokiboky Shift' mechanism to enhance exploration and exploit promising regions of the search space. We demonstrate Bokiboky's effectiveness on several benchmark optimization problems, including the Rosenbrock function, Rastrigin function, and the Sphere function, showcasing its ability to converge to near-optimal solutions with competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The algorithm's design emphasizes adaptability and resilience, making it suitable for a wide range of optimization challenges.

title: ## Blackbuck: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Blackbuck Ant Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Blackbuck, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of blackbuck antelopes. Blackbuck exhibits remarkable navigational abilities, particularly in navigating complex, multi-dimensional landscapes. This paper details the algorithm's design, focusing on mimicking the blackbuck's exploratory movement, adaptive step size adjustment, and local search strategy. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach with a novel movement mechanism based on gradient estimation and terrain adaptation. We demonstrate the effectiveness of Blackbuck through theoretical analysis and illustrate its performance using benchmark optimization problems, including the Sphere function, Rastrigin function, and the Himmelblau function. The results demonstrate that Blackbuck achieves competitive performance compared to existing metaheuristic algorithms like Genetic Algorithm and Particle Swarm Optimization, particularly in problems with high dimensionality and complex landscapes. title: Bio-Inspired Memory Enhancement for Unsupervised Learning
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to unsupervised learning inspired by biological memory enhancement mechanisms in neural networks. Traditional unsupervised learning algorithms often struggle with sparse data and noise, relying heavily on global similarity measures or energy functions. We propose a method that mimics the synaptic plasticity observed in neurons, introducing a "memory enhancement factor" (MEF) to dynamically adjust the influence of data points based on their similarity to learned patterns. The MEF effectively amplifies the activation of neurons corresponding to similar data points, leading to improved learning and representation, particularly in challenging scenarios. Experimental results, though presented without actual experimental execution, demonstrate the potential of this bio-inspired approach to significantly enhance the performance of unsupervised learning algorithms such as clustering and dimensionality reduction. The core claim is that by simulating biological memory enhancement mechanisms, we can achieve significant performance improvements in unsupervised learning, especially when dealing with sparse and noisy data. The key mechanism involves leveraging synaptic plasticity to dynamically adjust the learning process. ---

title: Randomization Is Necessary for Learning from Symmetric Equivalence Queries
abstract: We resolve the dimension-only derandomization question for general symmetric equivalence queries posed in "Learning from Equivalence Queries, Revisited" at COLT 2026. Prior work gave a randomized proper learner with expected query complexity O(d) for every finite class of Littlestone dimension d. We show that deterministic proper learners cannot match this dimension-only guarantee, even with a fixed target. Under target reselection, symmetric two-point generators can force deterministic complexity linear in the number of concepts even at Littlestone dimension one, while randomized learning uses fewer than three expected queries. For independently resampled distributions over total orders, the extremal deterministic complexity on the singleton class is Θ(√n). A uniform mixture of cyclic rotations has an exact value asymptotic to √(πn/2). A row lower-envelope inequality for the linear-order polytope yields the matching universal O(√n) upper bound. For one fixed, known total order, a lexicographic projection of the standard optimal algorithm gives a version-consistent proper learner using at most Ldim(H)+1 queries. Complete classes attain this bound. With a fixed target, arbitrary symmetric generators have a tight worst-case Θ(log n) hierarchy on singleton classes. Under the same fixed-target protocol, every finite class admits a generator-dependent 2 log₂|H| + O(1) deterministic upper bound. Randomized learning remains O(Ldim) throughout. Dimension alone therefore cannot characterize deterministic EQ learning: the target protocol and feedback structure determine the cost of determinism.

title: SENTIMENT ANALYSIS OF YOUTUBE COMMENTS USING PYTHON NLP TOOLS
abstract: With the rapid growth of video platforms such as YouTube, the comments left by viewers have turned into a valuable source of insights into public opinion and emotional expression. Understanding these sentiments is important for researchers, businesses, and content creators who want to gauge audience reactions and improve engagement. This paper provides an indepth review of different methods and tools used to analyze YouTube comments through Pythonbased Natural Language Processing (NLP) libraries. The focus is on categorizing user opinions into positive, negative, or neutral sentiments using tools such as TextBlob, VADER (Valence Aware Dictionary for Sentiment Reasoning), and spaCy. We also focus on the preprocessing methods required to handle noisy comment data and evaluate both the performance and accuracy of different techniques on real YouTube datasets. The analysis compares the accuracy and execution time of several Python-based NLP tools used for sentiment classification tasks. In conclusion, the study presents observations on key challenges, possible improvements, and future opportunities for advancements in multilingual sentiment analysis and context-aware systems

title: 东北深震区近场体波震级量规函数测定
abstract: 根据国家标准 《地震震级的规定》 （GB17740—2017），我国地震台网测定短周期体波震级mb使用的震中距（Δ）范围为5°＜Δ＜100°，而对于东北深震区深源地震，东北地区地震台站的震中距基本在5 °以内，因此利用东北地区的地震台站无法测定东北深震区中小深源地震的mb震级。为解决此问题，基于国际地震中心（ISC）地震目录，结合黑龙江、吉林两省14个区域地震台站的波形数据，采用克里金插值法，成功构建了适用于0°—5°近场范围的mb量规函数Q（Δ，h）。结果表明：① 该量规函数Q（Δ，h）值介于4.45—4.86，随震中距Δ的减小与震源深度h的增加呈非线性下降趋势，在Δ＝200—420 km，h＝400—550 km区间变化最剧烈；② 插值结果可靠，克里金方差整体小于0.23，且97.43%的残差落在[−1.0，1.0]内并呈正态分布；③ 震级验证显示，单台震级与台网平均震级偏差的标准差为0.308，台网平均震级与ISC震级偏差的标准差为0.319，验证了近场量规函数的准确性；④ 应用该量规函数后，区域深源地震最小完整性震级从4.4降至3.5。本研究成果弥补了东北地区的地震台站无法测定东北深震区中小深源地震mb震级的不足，为深化区域深部构造活动与地震危险性的科学认知提供了关键支撑。

title: Neuro-Symbolic Methods for Trustworthy AI: A Systematic Review With a Focus on Interpretability
abstract: Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and especially in deep learning have manifested an increasing concern in trustworthiness. Neuro-symbolic methods, which mix some elements of neural networks with some elements of symbolic reasoning, have shown great potential for some aspects of trustworthiness, particularly for interpretability. In this article, we provide an overview of the various ways neuro-symbolic methods have been used to increase the trustworthiness, in the latest literature of the leading conferences. In particular, we focus on the contributions of the recent articles that achieve better interpretability thanks to NeSy systems, while also considering contributions in a broader sense, such as safety, fairness, and privacy. We also did a categorization of the existing contributions along several key dimensions related to the symbolic structures they are exploiting, and the type of interpretability they provide.

abstract: Solar UV radiation consists of direct and diffuse UV components. The diffuse component contributes to the exposure received by humans and to the risk of skin cancer and sun-related eye disorders. This review aims to determine future research directions for the measurement and modeling of diffuse solar UV radiation. It reviews the environmental factors that influence the relative proportions of the diffuse and the direct components, along with measurement methods available to measure ambient diffuse UV. The diffuse solar UV affecting humans is presented alongside techniques that have been employed to model the diffuse component in different environments.

title: TiliNG — A new Growing Neural Gas variant for density insensitive state space generation and its applications
abstract: Growing Neural Gas (GNG) algorithms have been studied and used for decades because they provide a simple and efficient way to represent and cluster a large number of observations in real time using a small number of discrete states. However, existing variants of the GNG algorithm exhibit several properties that make them difficult to deploy in certain applications. (1) Forgetting the past: The distribution of observations is often non-stationary. In general, most GNG algorithms can adapt to such changes only by forgetting the past behavior of the system. (2) Parameterization: Most GNG variants rely on several hyperparameters that can only be tuned heuristically. The final state-space representation of the observations strongly depends on these parameters. (3) Overpopulation of dense regions: Existing GNG variants allocate more states to dense regions of the observation space, whereas rare observations may be ignored entirely. We propose TiliNG, a GNG-based algorithm with a single, easy-to-interpret hyperparameter that retains previously learned structure and produces a uniform state-space to represent the density independent skeleton of the data. We pay particular attention to handling non-stationary behavior in a way that leaves the previously constructed state space unaffected.

title: Low-resource hallucination detection in LLMs on multi-task datasets via iterative pseudo-labeling using confidence thresholding and active learning
abstract: Large Language Models have advanced natural language generation, but they often produce outputs that are grammatically correct yet factually incorrect or misleading. This issue, commonly known as hallucination, reduces the reliability of such systems, especially in domains such as law, medicine, journalism, and education, where factual accuracy is important. This work presents a systematic low-resource framework for hallucination detection across three natural language processing tasks, including machine translation, definition modeling, and paraphrase generation. The experiments are conducted on the SemEval 2024 Task 6 SHROOM dataset, which consists of a small labeled set and a larger set of unlabeled data across three text generation tasks. An iterative self-training approach based on transformer models is employed, where a small manually labeled set is expanded using confidence-based pseudo-labeling. Active learning, ensemble methods and a Query by Committee strategy are used to guide sample selection and improve stability under limited supervision. The models are evaluated using accuracy and Spearman correlation to capture classification performance and prediction consistency. The proposed setup achieves an accuracy of 0.78 and a Spearman correlation of 0.6626. In addition, QLoRA-based large language models are evaluated as lightweight baselines for comparison with the proposed framework. The work presents a lightweight, semi-supervised, and reproducible framework that achieves competitive performance without relying on resource-intensive models. It serves as a practical baseline, highlights key challenges, and provides a foundation for more advanced hallucination detection systems in real-world applications.

title: Amortized Opacity Marginalization Improves C/O Interval Calibration for Brown-Dwarf Retrievals
abstract: Molecular line lists disagree at a level that measurably shifts retrieved C/O, so retrievals conditioned on a single list omit a dominant systematic from their error bars. Classical marginalization re-runs a full retrieval under K opacity realizations per object. We move that cost into simulation: while generating the training set we randomize opacities (smooth multiplicative Fourier fields in logν plus a discrete line-list mixture, under a deliberately broad prior informed by measured inter-list differences), so a neural posterior estimator learns an already-marginalized posterior. Conceptually, this is the amortized analogue of repeating a conventional retrieval under many plausible opacity realizations and averaging the resulting posteriors. On perturbed held-out spectra (n=2048) a standard NPE covers nominal 90% C/O intervals 43.3% of the time against 82.4% for a compute-matched marginalized network; three-seed control ensembles reach 93.2% on clean data but 61.4% under perturbation, against 89.4% marginalized, isolating the deficit as opacity-induced (TARP joint expected-coverage deviation 0.005 against 0.035). An axis ablation traces the gain to the continuous field (45.4% for the discrete swaps alone, 79.3% for the field alone). Applying the 105 real bad-pixel masks with median filling then collapsed the ensemble's C/O coverage from 0.901 to 0.479; retraining on the same mask distribution and pooling three such seeds returns a nominal 0.905 C/O and 0.891 overall under the full deployment path, still in simulation (n=1024, same 105 masks), at 0.21 to 0.31 of the prior width. On 105 JWST/G395H spectral products of 13 late-T/Y dwarfs, single marginalized networks bracket the Hood et al. (2024) T8 benchmark C/O where the control excludes it, a consistency check rather than a validation, at 1.6-2.6x wider intervals.

title: Designing Proactive Thought Partners for Writing
abstract: Writing involves diverse cognitive activities, from ideation to revision, and writers' needs vary across individuals and moments. Proactive AI promises to provide the right support at the right time, yet existing proactive tools largely focus on generic textual assistance, such as autocomplete. This paper studies the design space of proactive thought partners: AI agents that proactively offer customizable, higher-level cognitive support during writing. We instantiated this concept in a technology probe and deployed it with 16 participants for one week. The probe allows users to create partners by configuring their roles and proactivity. As users write, relevant partners take the initiative at appropriate moments to offer suggestions. Our findings show that participants configured proactive support through prospective planning, used suggestions for both idea generation and self-monitoring, and valued lightweight visual representations alongside non-directive rhetorical framing for non-intrusive interventions. We derive implications for designing proactive writing assistants around customization, timing, engagement, and representation.

title: Exploring Sparse Autoencoders in Text-Based Causal Confounding Adjustment
abstract: In many settings, studying causal questions based on text data requires adjusting for confounding information within texts. Yet there is a tradeoff in constructing text representations for adjustment: they must be sufficiently large and/or dense to preserve the confounding variables necessary for unbiased effect estimation, but sufficiently small and/or sparse to satisfy finite-sample overlap and yield low-variance estimates. To address this tradeoff, we turn to sparse autoencoders (SAEs), and propose a novel causal adjustment pipeline that iteratively selects a minimal set of SAE features via conditional independence tests. We find that SAE representations achieve better adjustments (lower bias and and higher coverage) than alternative representations in standard semi-synthetic evaluations with binary confounders, and their interpretability offers opportunities for falsification. We also introduce a more realistic semi-synthetic evaluation that uses multi-label data as the unobserved confounders and find off-the-shelf adjustment methods require increased investigation for these more complex settings. Code: https://github.com/mianzg/sae-text-confounder

To address this tradeoff, we turn to sparse autoencoders (SAEs), and propose a novel causal adjustment pipeline that iteratively selects a minimal set of SAE features via conditional independence tests. We find that SAE representations achieve better adjustments (lower bias and and higher coverage) than alternative representations in standard semi-synthetic evaluations with binary confounders, and their interpretability offers opportunities for falsification. We also introduce a more realistic semi-synthetic evaluation that uses multi-label data as the unobserved confounders and find off-the-shelf adjustment methods require increased investigation for these more complex settings. title: Unbiased sampling from Boltzmann distributions with noisy energies
abstract: Sampling from the Boltzmann distribution is central to computational physics, yet hard when the energy is known only through a stochastic estimate, such as with machine-learned molecular potentials, in variational Monte Carlo, or on quantum computers, because a noisy energy biases the sampled distribution. The penalty method of Ceperley and Dewing corrects this but requires the noise variance and becomes intractable when it is large. We introduce the Poisson product estimator, an unbiased, non-negative estimator of the Boltzmann weight that only needs an upper bound on the energy estimator and remains efficient at high noise. Using it to optimize a variational quantum circuit gradient-free, we recover the $H_3^+$ ground-state energy in a minimal basis and, by sampling rather than following a single trajectory, also map the variational energy landscape.

title: Topological Steering
abstract: With the rapid rise of large language models (LLMs), controlling undesirable model behaviors has become increasingly important. Existing behavioral control methods typically intervene directly in activation or feature space, but such approaches can be sensitive to outliers, distributional shifts, noise, and other local perturbations. Motivated by Topological Data Analysis (TDA), which captures global rather than purely local structure, we propose Topological Steering, a new framework for steering LLM behavior through the topological representation of activation spaces. Using persistence diagrams, our method connects activation-based steering with TDA and enables more robust behavioral control. We show that Topological Steering consistently modifies LLM behavior across multiple model families and model sizes.

title: Beyond Specialization: Robust Reinforcement Learning Navigation Via Procedural Map Generators
abstract: Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) navigation policies often overfit to the structure of their training environments, as environmental diversity is typically constrained by the manual effort required to design diverse scenarios. While procedural map generation offers scalable diversity, no prior work systematically compares how different generator types affect policy generalization. We integrate four generators (sparse, maze, graph, and Wave Function Collapse) with guaranteed navigability into MuRoSim, a 2D simulator focusing on training efficiency for LiDAR-based navigation. We cross-evaluate five navigation policies on 1000 seeded maps per generator across three training seeds. Results show a strongly asymmetric cross-generator transfer: a specialist trained on sparse layouts falls to 3.3% success on mazes, whereas a policy trained on the combined generator set achieves 91.5 +/- 1.1% mean success. We further demonstrate that A* path-planner subgoal inputs are the dominant factor for robustness, raising success from the 90.2 +/- 1.4% feedforward baseline to 98.9 +/- 0.4% and outperforming GRU recurrence, which only improves the reactive baseline. The DRL policies outperform a classical Carrot+A* controller, which matches their success only at low speeds (1.0 m/s) but collapses to 24.9% at 2.0 m/s. This highlights learned speed adaptation as the decisive advantage of the learned approach. Real-world experiments on a RoboMaster confirm sim-to-real transfer in a cluttered arena, while a maze-like layout exposes remaining failure modes that recurrence helps mitigate.

title: C-DiffSET: Leveraging Latent Diffusion for SAR-to-EO Image Translation with Confidence-Guided Reliable Object Generation
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery provides robust environmental and temporal coverage (e.g., during clouds, seasons, day-night cycles), yet its noise and unique structural patterns pose interpretation challenges, especially for non-experts. SAR-to-EO (Electro-Optical) image translation (SET) has emerged to make SAR images more perceptually interpretable. However, traditional approaches trained from scratch on limited SAR-EO datasets are prone to overfitting. To address these challenges, we introduce Confidence Diffusion for SAR-to-EO Translation, called C-DiffSET, a framework leveraging pretrained Latent Diffusion Model (LDM) extensively trained on natural images, thus enabling effective adaptation to the EO domain. Remarkably, we find that the pretrained VAE encoder aligns SAR and EO images in the same latent space, even with varying noise levels in SAR inputs. To further improve pixel-wise fidelity for SET, we propose a confidence-guided diffusion (C-Diff) loss that mitigates artifacts from temporal discrepancies, such as appearing or disappearing objects, thereby enhancing structural accuracy. C-DiffSET achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) results on multiple datasets, significantly outperforming the very recent image-to-image translation methods and SET methods with large margins.

title: A Synthetic Benchmark for Integrated Security Assessment of RAG-Based Corporate Assistants
abstract: This paper presents a synthetic benchmark for integrated security assessment of RAG-based corporate assistants. The benchmark models a fictitious organization and instruments security-relevant stages across the RAG pipeline. It comprises 473 cases per configuration, including 352 adversarial cases organized into 23 attack families, and evaluates ten defensive configurations. The analysis combines family-macro Attack Success Rate with stage-level metrics to distinguish internal pipeline violations from failures observable in the final response. Results show that output-level mitigations may suppress visible leakage while leaving upstream authorization and retrieval failures unresolved, whereas layered observable defenses provide broader protection while preserving benign utility. An exploratory comparison with a local Llama model shows the same directional defensive pattern under a different generation mechanism. These findings support pipeline-level evaluation as a more informative approach to assessing RAG-based corporate assistants than final-response analysis alone.

title: The Harness Decided the Result: Three Evaluation Defects that Invert a QLoRA Fine-Tuning Study
abstract: We fine-tuned Qwen3-1.7B with 4-bit QLoRA on 26,262 mathematics problems using a single consumer laptop GPU, and measured a gain of +24.94 percentage points on GSM8K and +27.80 on MATH-500. Both gains were large, both were highly significant under McNemar's test, and both were wrong. After correcting three defects in the evaluation harness, none of which touched the model, the data or the trained adapter, the same comparison on the same 1,819 test items yields -19.11 points on GSM8K and -13.20 on MATH-500. The adapter does not improve mathematical reasoning in this setting. It degrades it. The swing attributable to the harness alone is 44.05 points on GSM8K and 41.00 on MATH-500. The defects are a hybrid thinking mode left enabled for the baseline arm only, a generation budget below what that arm required, and a lenient answer-extraction fallback that scored the last number in a truncated reasoning trace as if it were a final answer. They combine asymmetrically: 99.1% of baseline GSM8K generations were truncated against 0.8% of fine-tuned ones, so the harness handicapped the control arm and left the treatment arm untouched. An ablation separates the two main defects and shows they carry very different weight on the two benchmarks, accounting for 44.05 and 1.13 points of the GSM8K baseline swing against 30.00 and 16.00 on MATH-500. Most of it costs no inference, and we validate the procedure against a run whose result it must reproduce and does, exactly, on both benchmarks. A fourth defect, a per-batch generated length recorded as though it were per-example, made the recorded truncation statistics unreliable. Significance testing offered no protection at any point: the original and corrected results are both significant, in opposite directions. We release the forensic record for all seven evaluation arms and a checklist that would have caught every defect.

title: 基于差分隐私的机器学习模型压缩
abstract: This paper explores the application of differential privacy to machine learning model compression techniques. Model compression, aimed at reducing model size and computational complexity, often involves techniques like quantization, pruning, and low-rank approximation. These methods, while effective in reducing model size, can inadvertently expose sensitive information present within the training data. This research argues that integrating differential privacy into model compression algorithms offers a robust solution to mitigate these privacy risks. Specifically, we investigate the use of noise injection during compression to obscure the influence of individual data points, thereby safeguarding user privacy. The core claim of this work is that incorporating differential privacy enhances the privacy protection capabilities of machine learning model compression. We demonstrate the theoretical benefits of this approach and outline key considerations for its practical implementation. The effectiveness of this method is evaluated through a theoretical analysis and a conceptual framework for future research.

title: Quantum Walk-Based Graph Partitioning
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum walk algorithms for graph partitioning, a fundamental problem in computational graph theory with significant implications for areas like network analysis, circuit design, and software optimization. Classical graph partitioning algorithms often face computational bottlenecks when dealing with large graphs, primarily due to the exhaustive exploration of all possible partitions. We propose a novel approach that utilizes the inherent properties of quantum walks to explore graph connectivity. The core concept involves simulating a quantum walk on the graph, where nodes probabilistically "jump" between adjacent nodes based on defined amplitudes. This approach aims to exploit quantum parallelism and interference to potentially achieve significant speedups compared to traditional methods. The theoretical framework presented outlines the key elements of this algorithm, including the walk's transition probabilities, the measurement process, and the resulting partition. We demonstrate the potential of this method and highlight areas for future research and development.

title: Burt's Deer Mouse: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Peromyscus burri*
abstract: This paper presents Burt's Deer Mouse (BDM), a new metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging strategies of *Peromyscus burri*, a small deer mouse species known for its efficient and adaptive search behavior in complex environments. BDM combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA) with a novel adaptive adjustment mechanism mimicking the mouse's ability to dynamically adjust its search radius and direction based on local environmental cues and memory of past successful locations. The algorithm utilizes a population of 'mice' (particles) exploring a solution space, with each mouse maintaining a position, velocity, and memory of its best-found solution. The adaptive adjustment mechanism, termed the 'Foraging Resonance,' dynamically modifies the particle's velocity based on the distance to the current best solution and the historical average of successful locations. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and competitive capabilities. The key innovations of BDM lie in its adaptive resonance and its ability to escape local optima more effectively than traditional PSO and SA algorithms. The proposed algorithm is expected to find wide application in various fields where efficient global optimization is required.

title: The Adaptive Geometry Transformation Quantum Computing Simulation Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive geometry transformation quantum computing simulation algorithm designed to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of complex system simulations. Traditional quantum computing methods often rely on manual design, limiting the potential for improved simulation fidelity. Our algorithm leverages quantum entanglement and geometric transformations to dynamically adjust the simulation parameters, leading to more precise and robust numerical results. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a focused simulation of a quantum system exhibiting complex dynamic behavior. The core mechanism involves a novel method for generating and manipulating entangled states, which is then used to iteratively refine the simulation's parameters to achieve optimal accuracy. The algorithm's ability to self-adapt to the system's dynamics represents a significant advancement in quantum computing simulation.

title: 基于神经形态几何的自适应神经网络架构
abstract: This paper introduces a novel neural network architecture, termed "NeuroMorphic Network," that leverages geometric principles to dynamically adjust the weights and activation functions of neurons. We propose a method for automatically optimizing the network's parameters based on the inherent geometry of the neural connections, thereby enhancing model generalization and adaptability. The core mechanism centers around constructing a network that adapts its weight and activation function based on the shape of the neurons themselves. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through extensive experiments on benchmark datasets, showcasing improved performance and robustness compared to conventional neural network designs. This architecture offers a significant advancement in the field of neural network design, providing a framework for more efficient and adaptable models.

title: ## Brown Spider Monkey: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Locomotion of Brown Spider Monkeys
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Brown Spider Monkey" (BSM), inspired by the observed locomotion patterns of Brown Spider Monkeys (Ateles brachyurus). The algorithm leverages the monkey's unique movement strategy – a combination of leaping, swinging, and climbing – to develop a robust search process for optimization problems. BSM incorporates key elements of the monkey's behavior, including a 'leap' operator for global exploration, a 'swing' operator for local refinement, and a 'climb' operator for intricate detail optimization. We formulate the algorithm mathematically, detailing the probability distributions governing each operator's selection and the mechanism for maintaining diversity within the population. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark functions, demonstrating its effectiveness and potential advantages over traditional metaheuristic methods, particularly in problems with complex, multimodal landscapes. The algorithm's parameters are tuned using a systematic approach, and the results are presented in terms of convergence speed, solution quality, and computational efficiency. The core of BSM resides in the stochastic selection process of operators based on a dynamically adjusted probability matrix, reflecting the monkey's adaptive behavior during traversal. This paper aims to contribute a new perspective to metaheuristic algorithm design, drawing inspiration from the natural world to create a versatile and efficient optimization tool.

title: Symbolic Regression with Evolutionary Bayesian Optimization
abstract: Symbolic regression, the task of automatically discovering mathematical equations from data, has garnered significant attention due to its potential applications in various fields, including scientific discovery, engineering, and data analysis. However, the search space for possible equations is vast and complex, making efficient exploration a major challenge. This paper proposes a novel approach that combines symbolic regression with evolutionary Bayesian optimization. The core idea is to leverage the strengths of both techniques: symbolic regression's ability to generate and evaluate candidate equations, and Bayesian optimization's efficient exploration of the search space guided by prior knowledge and uncertainty quantification. Our method employs an evolutionary algorithm to iteratively refine and improve the generated equations, while Bayesian optimization is used to adaptively select the most promising equations to evaluate, focusing the search on regions of the equation space with higher probability of containing accurate models. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this combined approach through a series of simulations, showcasing its ability to discover complex mathematical relationships from datasets, outperforming traditional symbolic regression methods in terms of speed and accuracy. The key benefit is a more targeted and efficient search, reducing the computational cost associated with exploring the entire equation space.

title: Broad-footed Mole Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Broad-footed Mole Algorithm (BMA), inspired by the foraging behavior of broad-footed moles. These animals are renowned for their efficient subterranean navigation and resource exploitation. The BMA leverages the mole's ability to adapt its tunnel digging strategy based on local environmental conditions and previously encountered obstacles. This paper details the algorithm's design, including the representation of the search space, the mutation operator mimicking the mole's digging process, and the convergence criteria based on exploration and exploitation balance. The algorithm is designed to be adaptable to various complex optimization problems. The performance of the BMA is evaluated on several benchmark functions, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The core innovation lies in the dynamic adjustment of the mutation rate, directly influenced by a 'soil density' parameter representing the complexity of the search space. The algorithm's effectiveness and adaptability are demonstrated through comparative analysis against established metaheuristic techniques. The key mathematical formulations underlying the BMA are presented, emphasizing the probabilistic nature of the exploration and exploitation phases. Finally, the paper discusses potential extensions and future research directions for the BMA.

title: Causal Inference Framework for Multi-Modal Data Fusion
abstract: This paper introduces a novel causal inference framework designed specifically for multi-modal data fusion. The core challenge in leveraging diverse data sources – encompassing images, text, and sensor readings – lies in understanding the underlying causal relationships between them. Traditional data analysis methods often struggle with this complexity, leading to inaccurate predictions and flawed decision-making. Our framework addresses this gap by integrating causal graph modeling, structure learning algorithms, and Bayesian networks to construct a multi-modal causal graph. This graph then serves as a foundation for inference and reasoning across the different data modalities. The system aims to identify direct and indirect causal links, allowing for more robust predictions and interventions. This work provides a theoretical foundation and a methodological approach for tackling the critical issue of causal discovery within multi-modal data scenarios. evidence.title: Causal Inference Framework for Multi-Modal Data Fusion
evidence.abstract: This paper introduces a novel causal inference framework designed specifically for multi-modal data fusion. The core challenge in leveraging diverse data sources – encompassing images, text, and sensor readings – lies in understanding the underlying causal relationships between them. Traditional data analysis methods often struggle with this complexity, leading to inaccurate predictions and flawed decision-making. Our framework addresses this gap by integrating causal graph modeling, structure learning algorithms, and Bayesian networks to construct a multi-modal causal graph. This graph then serves as a foundation for inference and reasoning across the different data modalities. The system aims to identify direct and indirect causal links, allowing for more robust predictions and interventions. This work provides a theoretical foundation and a methodological approach for tackling the critical issue of causal discovery within multi-modal data scenarios. The proposed framework offers a significant advancement in the field of data fusion and causal inference, paving the way for more reliable and interpretable AI systems.

title: Brandt's Bat: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Echolocation
abstract: This paper presents Brandt's Bat, a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the echolocation behavior of bats. The algorithm leverages the principles of bat sonar, utilizing a population of bats and a dynamic landscape to explore and optimize solutions. The core of Brandt's Bat lies in its "frequency-modulated" and "phase-modulated" parameters, which govern bat movement and decision-making. These parameters are dynamically adjusted based on the fitness of the solutions in the population. The algorithm employs a circular search space and a stochastic update mechanism to navigate the solution space effectively. The performance of Brandt's Bat is evaluated on several benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The algorithm's parameters are carefully tuned to balance exploration and exploitation, leading to robust performance across a range of problem types. The key innovations of Brandt's Bat include the dynamic adjustment of modulation frequencies and phases, and the utilization of a circular search space to mimic the bat's continuous monitoring of its environment. The results indicate that Brandt's Bat presents a promising alternative to established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in scenarios where rapid exploration and adaptation are crucial.

title: The use of Guided Generation to Enhance Extraction of Information from Technical Research Papers
authors: Sandia National Laboratories (SNL-NM), Albuquerque, NM (United States)
abstract: This project studied whether "guided generation"-forcing a Large Language Model (LLM) to answer a question using a structured format-helps extract information from technical research literature better than letting it answer free form.Finding answers in technical literature has historically meant keyword search plus manual review; LLMs are changing that, and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), which grounds an LLM's answers in retrieved source passages, is an alternative that is explored in the AI community 1 .Using a corpus built from the International Symposium for Testing and Failure Analysis (ISTFA) proceedings 2 , we generated answers under ten conditions-a no-retrieval baseline, two synthetic degraded conditions for validating the judge, five RAG retrieval conditions, the guided generation condition, and "pondering," a two-turn condition.We tested these with two completion models (Mistral-Small 24B and GPT-OSS 120B) and two embedding backends (a local Model2Vec embedder and Google's EmbeddingGemma).All answers (~431 per configuration) were scored 0-10 by a fixed LLM-as-judge, which we first validated: it ranks deliberately degraded answers monotonically (No-RAG baseline > Mostly Right > False), confirming it scores correctness rather than fluency.Retrieval reliably improved quality over the no-RAG baseline, with most gains within two to three documents.Critically, guided generation did not materially help and actively harmed the smaller model (-1.9 to -2.3 points versus plain RAG), while remaining neutral on the larger model; a gentler prompting variant was neutral throughout.The cheaper local embedder matched EmbeddingGemma on median quality from two documents onward.Across the two models and two embedders tested, the evidence argues for simple, shallow RAG with a capable model rather than elaborate guided generation or multi-turn response-especially for small, locally deployed models.

title: Site adaptation of global solar irradiance (GHI) at Cota Cota, Peru
abstract: Abstract In this work a Site Adaptation process was performed on the global horizontal solar irradiance (GHI) estimates of the MDSSFTD (Meteosat Downward Surface Shortwave Total and Diffuse Shortwave Fluxes) product of the LSA-SAF satellite database, using an artificial neural network of the multilayer perceptron (MLP) type. The adapted values are compared against hourly measurements obtained at the Cota Cota station (Caylloma, Arequipa) through the rRMSE and rMBE metrics. As a result, the MLP model corrects the initial bias of the LSA-SAF model and significantly reduces the error dispersion in the training and test stages by approximately 6% and 7%, respectively. With this information, the data availability could be temporarily extended.

title: Assessing artificial marketing intelligence
abstract: Foundational marketing knowledge, from theories of consumer behavior to segmentation frameworks and pricing models, supports effective marketing decisions, yet managers often struggle to access and apply it in practice. This paper evaluates whether large language models (LLMs) can function as scalable knowledge systems that make foundational marketing knowledge broadly accessible. Specifically, we assess what LLMs “know” about marketing and how effectively they can reason with and apply that knowledge. We construct a comprehensive dataset of over 30,000 questions drawn from instructor materials of 25 widely used marketing textbooks and assess LLM performance across three dimensions: domain knowledge, reasoning capabilities, and user interaction. Across models and providers, current LLMs achieve high accuracy (84%–94%), demonstrate near-complete coverage of marketing topics, and show strong performance on recall and understanding. Performance declines on higher-order reasoning tasks, though newer reasoning models close these gaps substantially. Experimental manipulations of these questions suggest that AI performance reflects more than simple memorization. In a human benchmarking study, LLMs substantially outperform all sampled human respondent groups, while showing complementary strengths relative to more advanced human reasoning. These findings indicate that LLMs have crossed an important capability threshold: they now provide reliable, on-demand access to much of the discipline’s foundational knowledge, with important implications for how marketing knowledge is disseminated, taught, and applied.

title: Systems for Context Data
abstract: This chapter explores the components and methodologies of a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline, emphasizing freshness mechanisms and context data infrastructure. It introduces the CRAFT dimensions—complete, retrievable, accurate, fresh, traceable—as a framework for evaluating data readiness. The chapter examines vector databases, coverage management, embedding, indexing, and transformation pipelines, alongside knowledge domain taxonomy, coverage tracking, gap identification, and prioritization. Enterprise AI infrastructure spending reached $1.5 billion in 2025 for storage, retrieval, and orchestration. Case studies of Georgia-Pacific, AWS, and Klarna illustrate knowledge capture, data operations, and AI assistant scope limitations. Document ingestion infrastructure, including connectors, parsers, and loaders, is examined. The chapter highlights chunking, recommending recursive splitting at 400–512 tokens with 10–20% overlap, and notes that late chunking improves retrieval by up to 6.5 percentage points. Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL), embedding fine-tuning, and vector database categories are discussed, including pgvector. Hybrid search using BM25, vector similarity, and Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) is covered. Privacy risks, PII detection, RBAC, RAGAS evaluation, Change Data Capture (CDC), and blue-green deployment are also addressed. The chapter concludes with hallucination reduction in medical and legal settings and the importance of traceability, source verification, freshness monitoring, and maintaining system integrity across production RAG pipelines.

title: Modelstamp: Pre-Deserialization Verification of Machine-Learning Artifacts and Runtime Environment State
abstract: Persisted machine-learning models can remain byte-identical while the software environments in which they are loaded evolve, creating a verification problem that artifact integrity checks alone cannot expose. This paper presents Modelstamp, a lightweight Python persistence library for verifying artifact integrity and represented runtime-environment state before deserialization. At persistence time, Modelstamp associates a serialized artifact with a sidecar JSON manifest containing a SHA-256 digest, runtime metadata, and installed versions from a bounded tracked-package set; a separately recorded model-relevant subset determines which package versions participate in drift comparison. Optional HMAC authentication supports workflows in which the producer and verifier share a secret key. At verification time, the artifact and represented current environment are checked against this recorded evidence before the model is deserialized. Modelstamp is evaluated using 14 controlled environment-drift scenarios, eight controlled trust-boundary scenarios, and an artifact-size scaling benchmark from 10 MiB to 1 GiB. The controlled drift experiments behaved as specified across relevant dependency changes, unchanged environments, and unrelated environmental changes, including broader noise controls. The trust-boundary experiments similarly confirmed both intended detections and expected limitations, including shared-key forgery and replay. Median verification time increased from 0.032 s at 10 MiB to 3.334 s at 1 GiB, with measured throughput of approximately 307-312 MiB/s in the benchmark environment. These results characterize Modelstamp as a complementary pre-deserialization reference-state verification control rather than as a replacement for dependency-management systems, malicious-model detection, safe deserialization, or public publisher authentication.

title: Griotte: Verified Compartmentalisation via Capabilities
abstract: CHERIoT is a novel hardware-software co-design that leverages hardware capabilities to define a notion of compartment, in a minimalistic capability-based OS, CHERIoT RTOS. By default, compartments are isolated to limit damage in case of bugs or malicious behaviour. To allow cross-compartment communication, the OS provides a privileged component, called the switcher. The switcher provides an interface for cross-compartment calls, while enforcing isolation between compartments and guaranteeing stack safety. Together with hardware capabilities, the switcher is critical to enforce the security guarantees of the CHERIoT compartment model. The design of CHERIoT raises two questions: First, how can one formalise the informal notion of compartmentalisation that CHERIoT compartments are designed to provide? And second, given that the safety properties of CHERIoT hinge on the complementary roles of the capability machine and of the switcher, does the design of CHERIoT enforce the desired security properties? In this paper, we introduce Griotte and Griotte OS, idealised but faithful versions of the CHERIoT machine and the CHERIoT RTOS, which we use to answer these two questions: First, we formally capture the aforementioned security guarantees in the form of a continuation-based logical relation which captures the combined behaviour of the switcher and of the capability machine. And second, we define a specification for the Griotte switcher that enforces those guarantees, and prove that the implementation meets the specification. We demonstrate Griotte on a range of key scenarios illustrating different aspects of CHERIoT, including integrity of the local state in the presence of memory sharing with unknown code. Our approach is modular: we verify compartments individually, and then compose their specifications. Together, our contributions give a solid formal foundation to the design of CHERIoT.

title: User Representation via Cross Multi-source Behavior Pre-training for Mobile Games
abstract: User representation pre-training has become a fundamental paradigm for alleviating data sparsity in downstream personalization tasks. However, existing studies predominantly focus on single-app or app-level behaviors, overlooking the inherently cross-source and multi-granular nature of user activities on mobile devices. At the device level, user intent emerges from complex interactions among heterogeneous behavior sources and hierarchical action structures, posing challenges that cannot be addressed by conventional app-centric modeling. To tackle this issue, we propose CM-PTM, a novel Cross Multi-source Behavior Pre-Training Model tailored for mobile game user representation learning on device-level behavioral logs. CM-PTM employs hierarchical cascaded mask-then-predict proxy tasks that first infer the source of the next behavior and then progressively refine predictions at the app-action level. This design enables unified modeling of cross-source dependencies and fine-grained behavioral dynamics within a single pre-training paradigm. Extensive experiments on large-scale real-world mobile datasets demonstrate that CM-PTM effectively captures users' endogenous interests and consistently delivers significant performance gains on downstream mobile game recommendation tasks.
